- **Low**, `scripts/rename-plugin.sh:88-90` and `scripts/sync-core.sh:152-155`. The `.rename-new` and `.sync-core-new` files are left behind on interruption; `cleanup` removes only `TMP_FILE` and `LIST_FILE`. Track the file being written and remove it in `cleanup`.
- **Low**, `scripts/sync-core.sh:133-155`. Paths from the starter's `scripts/core-files.txt` are not checked; `../x` or `/x` would make `mkdir -p`, `cp` and `mv` write outside the plugin. Reject absolute paths and any `..` segment (die naming the line).
- **Low**, `scripts/sync-core.sh:137`. `cmp -s` ignores the file mode, so `--check` reports a match when only the executable bit differs. Compare the mode from `git ls-tree` (already read at `:153`) with the target's.

Declined: the `<PREFIX>_STARTER_DIR` help text (`:9`) uses the `STANDARDS.md` placeholder for the upper-case prefix, which is what the code reads; no tracked symlinks exist, so the copy-and-rename turning symlinks into files does not apply.

## Constraints

Core files. `scripts/rename-plugin.sh` must keep working on a fresh copy: after the change, try it on a throwaway clone (rename, lint, smoke test), as `AGENTS.md` asks. Must run on macOS bash 3.2 with BSD tools and Ubuntu. ShellCheck stays clean.

title: feat: plugin icon and banner on the Updates screen for GitHub updates
body:
## What

Plugins updated by the shared GitHub updater show WordPress's grey plug on the Updates screen (`update-core.php`) instead of their icon, and **View details** has no banner.

## Why

`includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php` `list_update()` sends `'icons' => array()`, and `plugin_information()` sends `'banners' => array()`. Core's `list_plugin_updates()` uses the first of `icons['svg']`, `['2x']`, `['1x']`, `['default']`, else the plug; `install_plugin_information()` uses `banners['low']`/`['high']` for the header. The listing images live only in `.wordpress-org/`, which `.distignore` leaves out of the zip, so a site has no copy.

## How

- Ship the icon: `scripts/build-banner.sh` also writes `admin/images/icon.svg` (plain SVG from `.wordpress-org/icon.svg`, about 6 KB), next to the `admin/images/banner.svg` it already writes.
- Updater: for each plugin it lists, look in the installed plugin's folder (`admin/images/`, `assets/`, `.wordpress-org/`) for WordPress.org's listing image names (`icon.svg`, `icon-256x256`, `icon-128x128`; `banner-1544x500`, `banner-772x250`, then `banner.svg`), and send their addresses as `icons` / `banners` in the update entry and in **View details**. Local files only: no request to GitHub when the screen loads, and private repositories work. Addresses without a scheme (`//host/...`) so an update check run from WP-CLI or cron (`is_ssl()` false) does not store `http:` addresses for an https admin.
- Raise the updater version in `includes/github-updater/load.php` (newest copy wins).
- `STANDARDS.md` (listing images, Updates from GitHub), `scripts/preflight-release.sh` checks `admin/images/icon.svg` is in Git when `.wordpress-org/icon.svg` is.
- Changelog and release (patch).

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`, `scripts/preflight-release.sh`.
- On a WordPress site with a GitHub build one version behind: the Updates screen shows the icon after **Check again**; **View details** shows the banner.

Plugins made from the starter pick it up with `scripts/sync-core.sh` (first: SEO Pro Stack).

title: fix: upstream active_plugins() leaving out deleted plugins (from SEO Pro Stack #521)
body:
## What

Upstream SEO Pro Stack's fix for wpallstars/seoprostack#521 into the starter's core file `includes/class-wpstarter-feature.php`: `active_plugins()` leaves out listed plugins whose files are gone, through a new `plugin_installed($file)` helper.

## Why

A plugin deleted while active stays in `active_plugins` until the Plugins screen is opened. The base feature then reports it active, so a feature that replaces it keeps waiting ("While that plugin is active, the feature waits"). SEO Pro Stack fixed this in its copy of the core file (commit 771ecc0, `GH#521: fix: a deleted plugin still listed as active no longer makes features wait`), so `scripts/sync-core.sh --check` there reports `includes/class-seoprostack-feature.php` as differing, and each sync would revert the fix (found while syncing for #376).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `includes/class-wpstarter-feature.php`
- EDIT: `README.md`
- EDIT: `changelog.txt`
- EDIT: `readme.txt`
- EDIT: `wp-plugin-starter-template.php`

## How

- In `includes/class-wpstarter-feature.php`, add before `active_plugins()`:
  - `public static function plugin_installed($file)`: `'' !== $file && 0 === validate_file($file) && is_file(WP_PLUGIN_DIR . '/' . $file)` (as `wp_get_active_and_valid_plugins()` checks), with its docblock.
  - In `active_plugins()`, keep a file only when `'.' !== $slug && self::plugin_installed($file)`; docblock line "Listed plugins whose files are gone are left out."
- Reference: SEO Pro Stack `includes/class-seoprostack-feature.php` at `main` (same code with `SEOProStack` names).
- Changelog (`README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`) and a patch release.

## What

title: fix: AI tool files reach release zips; Plugin Check fails GitHub-only direct endpoints
body:
## Problem

Found by Plugin Check on a plugin made from the starter:

1. AI tools write `.clinerules`, `.cursorrules`, `.windsurfrules` (pointers to `AGENTS.md`) and `MODELS.md` into each checkout. Nothing ignores them, so they get committed and reach both release zips, where Plugin Check fails `hidden_files`.

title: rename-plugin.sh: give new plugins a fresh pre-launch LAUNCH.md
body:
## Problem

`scripts/rename-plugin.sh` leaves `LAUNCH.md` as the starter's own launch state with only the names swapped. A new plugin's `LAUNCH.md` then says the repository is public, that the plugin "is not meant for WordPress.org" and "has no features", and lists a `main` ruleset, CodeQL, secret scanning and Scorecard as on. None of that is true for a new private plugin. Agents read `LAUNCH.md` (`STANDARDS.md:412`, `RELEASING.md:6,120,130`) and can act on the wrong state. Seen on a plugin made from v1.0.24, where `LAUNCH.md` had to be rewritten by hand after the first feature PR.

## Change

- `scripts/rename-plugin.sh`: next to the changelog reset in `set_version()` (lines ~206-217, `set_section` on readme.txt, changelog.txt and README.md), replace `LAUNCH.md` with a fresh pre-launch state for `$TO_NAME` at `$VERSION`:
  - in development, no release yet; the repository is private and making it public needs the owner's say;
  - while private: `DEVELOPMENT.md` → While private applies; no branch protection, rulesets, CodeQL, secret scanning or Scorecard (they need a public repository or a paid GitHub plan); Codacy, CodeFactor and SonarCloud are connected at public launch; `SYNC_PAT` is needed only once `main` is protected (`DEVELOPMENT.md` → Services setup, step 4);
  - at public launch: `DEVELOPMENT.md` → Secrets in history first, then `DEVELOPMENT.md` → At public launch, then update `LAUNCH.md` with what is on;
  - WordPress.org: not submitted; `RELEASING.md` → WordPress.org when the owner says, and record the submission here.
  Write it whole (the starter's text is not a template for a plugin's); keep the starter's own `LAUNCH.md` unchanged in this repository.
- Header comment (line 34): add `LAUNCH.md` to "Then update README.md, readme.txt, changelog.txt, AGENTS.md and the banner".
- `README.md` → "Start a plugin" step 3 (and `STANDARDS.md` if it lists the files to make the plugin's own): add `LAUNCH.md`.
- Do not add `LAUNCH.md` to `scripts/core-files.txt`; it is per plugin.

### Files Scope

- `scripts/rename-plugin.sh`
- `README.md`
- `STANDARDS.md`
- `changelog.txt`

Integration scope recovery: retain the prior PR #391 developer-tool changelog entry in `changelog.txt`, as required by STANDARDS.md Structure and the verified review finding. This adds only the existing Unreleased entry; preserve current-main entries. Collision discovery found no open related PR. Verification: scratch renaming, scripts/lint.sh and git diff --check.

title: GitHub updater: check GitHub again when core's update_plugins cache is cleared
body:
## What happened

On a live site running SEO Pro Stack, after publishing the v1.3.22 GitHub release:

```
wp transient delete update_plugins --network
wp plugin update seoprostack   # "Success: Plugin already updated."
wp plugin get seoprostack --field=version   # 1.3.21
```

The new release appeared only after also deleting the shared updater's own cache:

```
wp transient delete wpallstars_github_releases --network
wp plugin update seoprostack   # 1.3.21 -> 1.3.22 Updated
```

## Cause

`includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php`:

- `release()` (~line 404) answers from the `wpallstars_github_releases` site transient while `still_fresh()` (~line 439) holds: younger than `FRESH` (12 hours; an hour after a failure).
- `forced()` (~line 390) is the only bypass, and it only matches `update-core.php?force-check=1` in wp-admin.
- So clearing core's `update_plugins` transient, the usual way to make WordPress and WP-CLI check again, makes core ask again, but `add_updates()` (`pre_set_site_transient_update_plugins`, ~line 159) gets the cached GitHub answer. Up to 12 hours can pass before a new release shows.

## Proposed fix

Treat these as a forced check too, keeping the existing `RECENT` (one minute) guard so one check never fetches twice:

1. A core update check that starts with no stored `update_plugins` site transient (someone cleared it, or a fresh install). In `add_updates()`, or where `forced()` is decided, check whether `get_site_transient('update_plugins')` was empty when the check started. Note that core's `wp_update_plugins()` saves the transient twice in one check (once to stamp `last_checked`, then with the answers), so read that state once per request.
2. Optionally, WP-CLI update commands (`defined('WP_CLI') && WP_CLI` while `wp plugin update` / `wp plugin list --update=available` runs). Check what WP-CLI's `CommandWithUpgrade` calls first; item 1 may already cover it.

Keep GitHub requests bounded: normal page loads and cron must still use the 12-hour cache.

## Where to change it

- Master copy: `includes/github-updater/` in this starter repo. Raise the version in `includes/github-updater/load.php`, then copy the folder to each plugin made from the starter (`STANDARDS.md` → Updates from GitHub; e.g. wpallstars/seoprostack `scripts/core-files.txt` lists `includes/github-updater/`).
- Document the new behaviour in `STANDARDS.md` → Updates from GitHub (when the updater asks GitHub again).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php`
- EDIT: `includes/github-updater/load.php`
- EDIT: `STANDARDS.md`

## Verification

On a throwaway WordPress site with a plugin served by the updater and an older version installed:

1. Let the updater cache a release (visit Dashboard → Updates once).
2. Publish a newer release (or point the plugin at a repo whose latest release is newer than the cached answer).
3. `wp transient delete update_plugins --network && wp plugin update <slug>` must update without deleting `wpallstars_github_releases`.
4. Load ordinary admin pages and run `wp cron event run wp_update_plugins` several times: the updater makes at most one GitHub request per 12 hours (watch with `pre_http_request` logging or Query Monitor's HTTP panel).
5. `bash scripts/lint.sh` and the starter's Plugin Check pass.

title: Settings screen: header for a plugin's own screens, and instant tabs within a group
body:
## What

Two changes to the settings screen (core files), from a plugin that has its own top-level screen next to its settings:

1. **The header on a plugin's other screens.** A plugin with its own admin screen (a dashboard in its top-level menu, `WPStarter_Setup::MENU_PARENT`) should show the same header as the settings screen: name, version, feature search and the Source code / Support / Buy me a coffee links. Today the header markup is inside `WPStarter_Admin_Manager::render_settings_page()` and its styles are in the settings stylesheet, whose unscoped classes (`.wps-card`, `.wps-section`, `.wps-empty`) would restyle such a screen if it were loaded there.
2. **Instant tabs.** Each settings tab is a full page load. Switching between tabs in the same group (the tabs between two dividers in the navigation) should be instant: draw the group's tabs at once, show one, and switch with the address updated, so Back, reload and bookmarks still work.

## How

- `admin/css/wpstarter-header.css` (new core file): the screen's colour tokens, the full-width `.wps-wrap`, the header, the search field and notices under the header. The settings stylesheet depends on it.
- `WPStarter_Admin_Manager::render_header()` and `enqueue_header()`: public, for a plugin's own screens (`<div class="wrap wps-wrap">`, the header, `<hr class="wp-header-end">`, then its content). The search form shows only to people who can open the settings screen.
- `WPStarter_Admin_Manager::page_tabs()`: the active tab and the other tabs of its group that preload. Settings tabs and Read Me preload; tabs added with `wpstarter_admin_tabs` preload only with `'preload' => true`, as their scripts and markup may expect to be alone on the page.
- `wpstarter_admin_enqueue` and `wpstarter_admin_script_deps` run once for each tab on the page (active first); `wpstarterAdmin.tab` follows the shown tab and `wpstarterAdmin.tabs` lists the page's tabs; `wpstarter:tab-shown` fires on a switch.
- `admin/js/wpstarter-admin.js`: a Tabs controller. Plain clicks on a tab drawn on the page show its panel and `pushState` the tab's address; Back/Forward switch back; modified clicks open as usual.

## Files

- `admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php`, `admin/js/wpstarter-admin.js`, `admin/css/wpstarter-admin.css`, new `admin/css/wpstarter-header.css`, `scripts/core-files.txt`
- `README.md` (Developers, changelog), `changelog.txt`

## Verify

- `scripts/lint.sh`, `scripts/smoke-test.sh`
- In a plugin made from the starter: tabs in one group switch without a reload; the address, Back and reload follow; saving a setting on a switched-to tab works; the search results and other groups still load as pages; the header shows on the plugin's own screen with its own styles untouched.

title: sync-core.sh: keep a plugin own lines in marked blocks of core files
body:
## What

`scripts/sync-core.sh` replaces each core file whole, so a plugin that adds its own lines to a core file loses them on every sync. Give core files marked places for a plugin's own lines, and have `sync-core.sh` keep the plugin's lines there.

## Why

A plugin made from the starter documents its own check (a shop test for its purchases code) in three core files:

- `.distignore`: excluding its test fixture (`/scripts/shop-test-mu.php`) from release zips.
- `DEVELOPMENT.md`: a row in the checks table and a paragraph on how to run it.
- `RELEASING.md`: a release step to run it when purchases code changes.

Every `scripts/sync-core.sh` run deletes those 18 lines (seen on three syncs in a row). Each time they have to be noticed and reverse-applied by hand. If they are missed, the fixture ships in the zip and the release step disappears. `scripts/sync-core.sh --check` also lists those files as `differs` for good, which hides real drift.

## How

1. Add an empty block for the plugin's own lines at each place a plugin may extend a core file:
   - `.distignore`: after `/scripts`, as `# {css}-own:start` / `# {css}-own:end` comment lines.
   - `DEVELOPMENT.md`: after the checks table (`scripts/lint.sh with no arguments runs the first seven.`) and before "The scripts work out which plugin…", as `<!-- {css}-own:start -->` / `<!-- {css}-own:end -->`.
   - `RELEASING.md`: inside step 2 of the release steps (after the `scripts/plugin-check.sh` line), same HTML comments.
   - Use the starter's own prefix (`wps-own`); `plugin_map` renames it like the other names. One marker name for every file keeps the code simple.
2. In `scripts/sync-core.sh` `sync_file()`, after `plugin_map` writes `TMP_FILE`, if the target already exists and has `{css}-own:start`…`{css}-own:end` blocks, copy each block's inner lines into the matching (same-order) empty block in `TMP_FILE` before the `cmp`. `--check` then compares with the plugin's lines in place, so a plugin's own lines are no longer drift.
3. Stop with `die` (never drop lines silently) when the target has more `own` blocks than the starter's file, or a start marker has no end marker.
4. `STANDARDS.md` → Structure: one sentence saying a plugin's own lines in a core file go only between its `{css}-own` markers. The file is at the 500-line limit, so rewrite an existing line rather than adding one.
5. Changelog (`changelog.txt`, `README.md` → Unreleased): a Developers entry.

Reference pattern: `sync_file()` in `scripts/sync-core.sh` (TMP_FILE, `cmp`, rename-into-place); `plugin_map` for name mapping.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `scripts/sync-core.sh`
- EDIT: `.distignore`
- EDIT: `DEVELOPMENT.md`
- EDIT: `RELEASING.md`
- EDIT: `STANDARDS.md`
- EDIT: `changelog.txt`
- EDIT: `README.md`

## Verify

- `scripts/lint.sh` passes (ShellCheck: zero violations; `local var="$1"`; explicit returns).
- In a scratch plugin made with `scripts/rename-plugin.sh`, add lines inside the three `own` blocks, run `scripts/sync-core.sh --from <starter> --ref HEAD`: the lines are kept, and nothing else changes when the starter has not changed.
- Change a core line outside the blocks in the starter, sync again: that line updates and the plugin's lines stay.
- `scripts/sync-core.sh --check` reports no `differs` for a plugin whose only differences are inside its blocks.
- An unmatched start marker in the target makes the sync stop with a message and write nothing.

## Out of scope

Moving the plugin's lines into its marked blocks, which is done in the plugin after this ships.

title: feat: shared updater runs due update checks in WP-Cron, not on admin screens
body:
## What

Admin screens wait for update servers when WordPress's stored core, plugin or theme update check is 12 hours old: core runs `_maybe_update_core()`, `_maybe_update_plugins()` and `_maybe_update_themes()` on `admin_init`, so the next admin screen opened waits while WordPress and every plugin's own updater ask their servers (seconds on sites with many premium plugins).

The shared GitHub updater should run those due checks in WP-Cron instead, through core's own cron events (`wp_version_check`, `wp_update_plugins`, `wp_update_themes`), and leave them on admin screens while WP-Cron is not running.

## Why here

`STANDARDS.md` → Code rules: update behaviour changes only in the shared updater (Plugin Check `plugin_updater_detected`; WordPress.org asks plugins not to interfere). The updater is GitHub-build only (`.distignore-wporg`), so this reaches GitHub builds only. It replaces a hand-copied must-use file on the owner's sites, which never updated.

## Files

- `includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php`: `checks_in_cron()` on `admin_init` priority 1 from `boot()`, `check_due()`, filter `wpallstars_github_updater_checks_in_cron`.
- `includes/github-updater/load.php`: version 1.4.0.
- `STANDARDS.md`: update rule covers when and where checks run; Updates from GitHub bullet; Performance: admin screens do not wait on remote requests that can run in cron; clear only the plugin's own object-cache keys, never `wp_cache_flush()` (shared memcached on many hosts).
- `README.md`: What you get, filter, changelog.

## Verification

- `vendor/bin/phpcs includes/github-updater/` and `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse` pass.
- After syncing to a plugin and deploying: on a site, `admin_init` no longer has the three `_maybe_update_*` callbacks after the hook runs, and a due check schedules its cron event; the Plugins and Updates screens still check.

title: STANDARDS.md: spacing and form rules for admin screens
body:
## What Add a short **Admin screens: spacing and forms** rule set to `STANDARDS.md` (a core file, so plugins get it with `scripts/sync-core.sh`), so React forms and modals in wp-admin built from the starter have even spacing and aligned labels from the start. ## Why A plugin made from the starter shipped a modal form whose fields used WordPress components with their default bottom margins, mixed with plain `

`, `

` and `
    ` elements carrying browser margins. The result: uneven gaps, labels in side-by-side fields not lining up, a link notice with cramped content, and a disabled button and checkbox with no visible reason ("clicking this does nothing"). Each plugin rediscovers the same fix; the rules belong in the shared standard. ## Rules to add (our own words; adjust to the file's style) - WordPress form components (`TextControl`, `SelectControl`, `TextareaControl`, `CheckboxControl`, `ToggleControl`) get `__nextHasNoMarginBottom`; inputs, selects and the buttons beside them get `__next40pxDefaultSize`. Controls carry no outer margin of their own. - The container spaces its children: a form or group is `display: grid; gap: 16px`; related buttons `gap: 8px`; help text 4px under its field. Use WordPress's 4px scale (4, 8, 12, 16, 24). - Reset `margin: 0` on `p`, headings and lists inside such containers; never mix browser margins with `gap`. - Group fields with `
    ` and `` (legend `float: left; width: 100%` so it takes part in the grid), separated by a 1px `#dcdcde` top border, rather than headings with ad-hoc margins. - Short fields side by side: `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr)); align-items: start`, so labels line up and the row wraps on narrow screens. - Notices with content and actions: the notice content is a grid with `gap: 8px`; a read-only URL is a full-width monospace input with its buttons (Copy, Open in a new window) on one wrapping row. - A disabled control always says why: help text under it, or `accessibleWhenDisabled` with a `title`. A required field validates on submit with a message instead of a silently disabled submit button. - Modals use the plugin's modal class (fixed width at WordPress's small breakpoint and up, full-width sheet below) and end with right-aligned Cancel (tertiary) and the primary action. ## Files - `STANDARDS.md`: new subsection, probably next to **Front-end styling and dark mode** (exact placement is the implementer's call). - If the starter ships admin form CSS (path not verified; check `admin/` and `assets/`), add the matching utility classes (`.{css}-form`, `.{css}-fieldset`, `.{css}-form__row`, `.{css}-form__actions`) there so plugins inherit them. ### Files Scope - EDIT: `STANDARDS.md` ## Verification - `scripts/lint.sh` passes. - Markdown renders; the new rules use the file's placeholders (`{css}`, `{prefix}`) where names appear. - If CSS is added: a sample form screenshot at 1400px and 600px wide shows even gaps and aligned labels in two-column rows. --- [aidevops.sh](https://aidevops.sh) v3.38.31 plugin for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) v1.18.35 with claude-opus-5-5 spent 1d 10h and 7,108,412 tokens on this with the user in an interactive session.

## Task Brief

## What

Make `STANDARDS.md` more concise as a whole, without losing any rule or detail, so it gets back under 500 lines (it is 554 at 67b9d99, up from 500 three commits earlier: #401, #403, #404).

## Why

`STANDARDS.md` is a core file, copied word for word into every plugin made from the starter by `scripts/sync-core.sh`. Plugins cannot shorten their copy, so its size blocks their pushes: the aidevops pre-push file-size guard fails Markdown files other than READMEs over 500 lines, and a plugin's core-sync PR needed an owner-approved `COMPLEXITY_GUARD_DISABLE=1` to push. aidevops is tracking a higher limit for root Markdown files (marcusquinn/aidevops#34043), but a shorter, tighter standard is better for people and agents either way. #358 (PR #359) brought it under 500 lines once by moving preview-site details to `DEVELOPMENT.md`; this time, prefer concision across the whole document over moving more out.

1. Read the whole of `STANDARDS.md` first; edit for concision across the document, not by cutting the newest sections:
   - remove repetition between sections and with `DEVELOPMENT.md` / `RELEASING.md` (keep each rule in one place and point to it);
   - tighten wordy sentences; use lists or tables where they say the same in fewer lines;
   - keep every rule, number, name, path and example; nothing may be lost.
2. Only if a concise whole is still over 500 lines, move a self-contained section to a new core reference doc (add it to `scripts/core-files.txt`), link it, and update docs that link to the moved section. Otherwise leave `scripts/core-files.txt` unchanged.

- `scripts/core-files.txt`

- the starter's plug on the stack: the comment `The WordPress Plugins icon (Dashicons admin-plugins` in `.wordpress-org/banner.svg` or `.wordpress-org/icon.svg`;

Warnings, not errors: a person fixes them, and a plugin may keep a credit on purpose.

- [x] Memory recall: `starter rename-plugin preflight release checklist LAUNCH.md` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-09
- **Created by:** ai-interactive, at the maintainer's request
- **Conversation context:** A plugin made from the starter was taken from its first development version to a 1.0.0 release candidate. Most of the work was finding what still said "starter": the banner's headline and tagline, the plug on the banner and icon, the plugin's `Description:`, the readme's short description and opening, screenshots, and a release pass of every script. The maintainer asked for a checklist the starter gives every new plugin, so the next one does not rediscover it.

## What

1. Every plugin made with `scripts/rename-plugin.sh` gets a **Before 1.0** checklist in its `LAUNCH.md`: a short list of tickable items that take it from a renamed starter to a release-ready plugin (the list is in Implementation Steps).
2. `RELEASING.md` gets a short **First release** section that points to that checklist and says that `scripts/preflight-release.sh` warns about what is still the starter's.
3. `scripts/preflight-release.sh` gets a **Starter leftovers** section, skipped when the repository is the starter itself, that warns when a plugin still has:
   - the starter's banner words: `Built with AI` as the banner headline, or the tagline `A clean start for WordPress plugins` in `.wordpress-org/banner.svg`;
   - the starter's plug on the stack: the comment `The WordPress Plugins icon (Dashicons admin-plugins` in `.wordpress-org/banner.svg` or `.wordpress-org/icon.svg`;
   - the starter's description: `A clean start for a WordPress plugin` in the main file's `Description:` header or as `readme.txt`'s short description;
   - the starter's screenshots: a `.wordpress-org/screenshot-N.png` whose Git blob id equals the starter's at the same path (compare against the blob ids of the starter's `screenshot-1.png` and `screenshot-2.png` at release time, written into the script as constants).
   Warnings, not errors: a person fixes them, and a plugin may keep a credit on purpose.

## Why

`rename-plugin.sh` renames the plugin but cannot write its offering, its picture or its screenshots, and nothing tells the maker which starter text survives. Preflight passed (0 errors) on a plugin whose banner still said "Built with AI / A clean start for WordPress plugins" and whose icon still showed the starter's plug. A checklist plus leftover warnings make the release path explicit and checkable.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: scripts/rename-plugin.sh:186-252` — in the `LAUNCH.md` heredoc written by `set_version()`, add `## Before 1.0` after `## While private` with the checklist below (Markdown `- [ ]` items, the same short plain style as the rest of the file).
- `EDIT: scripts/preflight-release.sh` — add `check_starter_leftovers()` modelled on `check_agent_docs()` (780–821): `section "Starter leftovers"`, `git show "$sha:<path>"` reads, `warn` per finding, one `ok` when clean, `return 0`. Skip with a `note` when `[[ "$PLUGIN_REPO" = "$STARTER_REPO" ]]` (the same test `check_agent_docs()` uses at line 798). Call it in `main()` beside `check_agent_docs "$sha"` (line 1027).
- `EDIT: RELEASING.md` — add `## First release` before `## WordPress.org` (line 107): three or four lines pointing to the `LAUNCH.md` checklist and the Starter leftovers section of preflight.
- `EDIT: README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt` — changelog entries in the starter's convention (`STANDARDS.md` → the rule at line 123: `README.md` feature notes and changelog, `changelog.txt` user-facing entry, `readme.txt`). It is a "Developers:" change; nothing changes for users.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `LAUNCH.md` is written only by `set_version()` in `scripts/rename-plugin.sh`; preflight sections are called only from `main()` in `scripts/preflight-release.sh`; `.github/workflows/release.yml` runs preflight on tags (warnings do not fail it).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** the heredoc in `set_version()` → `replace_with_tmp LAUNCH.md`. No other writer.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `scripts/lint.sh` (ShellCheck on both scripts); running preflight on the starter and on a renamed copy (Verification below).
- **Schemas/config:** none; `scripts/core-files.txt` already lists both scripts and `RELEASING.md`, so `scripts/sync-core.sh` carries the change to plugins.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** none.
- **Migrations/backfills:** existing plugins keep their `LAUNCH.md`; `sync-core.sh` does not overwrite it (it is not a core file). They get the leftover warnings through the synced preflight script.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the PR.

### Implementation Steps

1. The checklist in the `LAUNCH.md` heredoc (keep the wording short; `$TO_NAME` and other variables are already in scope there):

```markdown
## Before 1.0

Tick these off; `scripts/preflight-release.sh` checks most of them.

- [ ] Description: the `Description:` header and `readme.txt`'s short description (150 characters at most) say what this plugin does, not the starter's.
- [ ] `README.md` and `readme.txt` open with this plugin's own offering (what it does, for whom, why it differs), then getting started and a guide. Keep both credits (Built with AI, Made from).
- [ ] `readme.txt`: under 10 KB, up to 5 tags, Tested up to the latest WordPress, FAQ, an External services section for every service the plugin contacts, one Screenshots caption per screenshot.
- [ ] Banner and icon: in `.wordpress-org/banner.svg` replace the headline and tagline, and replace the starter's plug on the stack with this plugin's own mark (the same in `.wordpress-org/icon.svg`); run `scripts/build-banner.sh` and check the icon reads at 128 px.
- [ ] Screenshots of this plugin in `.wordpress-org/screenshot-N.png` (`scripts/build-banner.sh` makes the View details copies).
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` describes this plugin; `DESIGN.md` and search keywords, if the plugin has them, are current.
- [ ] Version 1.0.0 everywhere: `Version:`, the version constant, `Stable tag:`, `README.md`'s Version line and the three changelogs.
- [ ] `scripts/sync-core.sh --check` lists no differences from the starter.
- [ ] Checks pass: `scripts/lint.sh`, `scripts/preflight-release.sh` (no errors; each warning understood), `scripts/smoke-test.sh`, `scripts/plugin-check.sh` (no errors on either zip).
- [ ] The owner has seen it on a test site (`scripts/preview-site.sh`) and approved the banner, icon and screenshots.
- [ ] WordPress.org: if the Plugin Name gives another slug, ask for this plugin's slug in the submission notes.
- [ ] After the release: `scripts/update-test.sh`.
```

2. `check_starter_leftovers()` skeleton (Bash 3.2; `local var="$1"`; explicit `return 0`; keep it under ~60 lines, splitting a helper for the screenshot comparison if needed):

```bash
check_starter_leftovers() {
	local sha="$1"
	local plugin_header="$2"
	local readme="$3"
	section "Starter leftovers"
	if [[ "$PLUGIN_REPO" = "$STARTER_REPO" ]]; then
		note "this is the starter"
		return 0
	fi
	local problems=0 banner icon
	banner="$(git show "$sha:.wordpress-org/banner.svg" 2>/dev/null || true)"
	icon="$(git show "$sha:.wordpress-org/icon.svg" 2>/dev/null || true)"
	# ... grep -qF each marker from What step 3; warn naming the file and what to replace; problems=1
	# ... field "$plugin_header" "Description" and the readme short description vs the starter's
	# ... git rev-parse "$sha:.wordpress-org/screenshot-N.png" vs the starter's blob ids
	[[ "$problems" -eq 1 ]] || ok "no starter banner words, plug, description or screenshots"
	return 0
}
```

   Pass the same `plugin_header` and `readme` values `main()` already passes to `check_readme`/`check_wporg_assets`; read `main()` (965–1046) for their variable names. Write the starter's marker strings so `rename-plugin.sh`'s replacements cannot rewrite them in a renamed plugin, the same way `STARTER_REPO` is split at line 36 (for example split `"A clean start for ""WordPress plugins"`), because rename replaces the starter's name and repository across files.

3. `RELEASING.md` → `## First release`, then the changelog entries, then run Verification.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** none; read-only checks and a heredoc written through `replace_with_tmp`.
- **Migration/rollback:** existing plugins get only the new warnings; revert removes them.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** plugins synced before this change keep their old `LAUNCH.md`; the checklist reaches them only if they copy it (say so in the changelog note).
- **Idempotency/retry:** preflight is read-only; rerunning `rename-plugin.sh` rewrites `LAUNCH.md` as before.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** a missing banner or icon file is not a leftover (`check_wporg_assets` already warns); `|| true` on the `git show` reads.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
scripts/lint.sh
scripts/preflight-release.sh          # on the starter: "Starter leftovers" says "this is the starter", no new warnings
scripts/rename-plugin.sh --slug leftover-test --name "Leftover Test" --prefix LeftoverTest --repo example/leftover-test
scripts/preflight-release.sh          # warns for the banner words, plug, description and screenshots
```

- **Surface mapping:** lint proves ShellCheck/Bash 3.2 style; the starter run proves the skip; the renamed-copy runs prove each marker is found and cleared; reading the generated `LAUNCH.md` proves the checklist is written.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required — two core scripts and docs; the release workflow runs preflight on tags anyway.

### Files Scope

- `scripts/rename-plugin.sh`
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh`
- `RELEASING.md`
- `README.md`
- `changelog.txt`
- `readme.txt`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A plugin made with `scripts/rename-plugin.sh` has `## Before 1.0` in its `LAUNCH.md` with the checklist items above.

  ```yaml

    method: codebase
    pattern: "## Before 1.0"
    path: "scripts/rename-plugin.sh"
  ```

- [ ] `scripts/preflight-release.sh` has a Starter leftovers section that warns, on a renamed copy, about the starter's banner words, plug, description and screenshots, and stops warning once each is replaced.

  ```yaml

    method: codebase
    pattern: "check_starter_leftovers"
    path: "scripts/preflight-release.sh"
  ```

- [ ] On the starter itself preflight adds no warning or error (the section notes "this is the starter"), and the result of a starter release check is unchanged otherwise.
- [ ] Leftover findings are warnings only: preflight's error count, and so the Release workflow, is not affected.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: manual
    prompt: "Run scripts/preflight-release.sh on the starter and on a renamed copy; confirm 0 new errors in both, warnings only in the copy."
  ```

- [ ] `RELEASING.md` has `## First release` pointing to the checklist; changelog entries follow `STANDARDS.md`.
- [ ] `scripts/lint.sh` passes (ShellCheck clean, explicit returns, `local var="$1"`).

## Context & Decisions

- Checklist in each plugin's `LAUNCH.md` (per plugin, tickable, already reset by `rename-plugin.sh` since #390) rather than a core doc: core files are overwritten by `sync-core.sh`, so ticks there would be lost.
- Warnings, not errors: the starter cannot know when a plugin intends to keep something (for example a credit line that mentions the starter).
- Not in scope: generating a plugin's banner art, writing its readme, or changing `scripts/build-banner.sh`.
- Public repository: keep examples generic; do not name private plugins or local paths.

- `scripts/preflight-release.sh:780-821` — `check_agent_docs()`, the pattern (starter skip at 798).

## Task


One README badge block for every plugin made from the starter, written by the starter and kept that way: three rows on GitHub, the same in every plugin.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

Target repository: wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding

## What

One README badge block for every plugin made from the starter, written by the starter and kept that way: three rows on GitHub, the same in every plugin.

## Why

Three tools write the block between `<!-- aidevops:badges:start -->` and `<!-- aidevops:badges:end -->`, each with its own layout:

- `scripts/rename-plugin.sh` → `set_badges()` (three rows: status, size, languages chart).
- aidevops `badges sync` (`badges-sync-helper.sh`, `readme-badges-helper.sh`), which replaces the block with grouped sections (`<!-- Build & Quality Status -->`, `<!-- License & Legal -->`, …), each followed by a blank line.
- aidevops `wp_plugin_quality.py` (new-plugin workflow), which strips and adds hosted-service badges.

SEO Pro Stats ended up with the aidevops layout on GitHub: every group was its own paragraph, the 520×96 languages chart (`docs/metrics/badges/languages.svg`) sat inline beside the 20px lines-of-code badge, so the rows stacked and misaligned, and the chart's white background (`<rect … fill="#ffffff"/>`) is a bright panel in GitHub's dark mode. A "github repository" badge linked to the page it is on. Fixed by hand in wpallstars/seoprostats (see `README.md` lines 5–20 there); nothing stops the next sync from writing it back.

## How

1. In `scripts/rename-plugin.sh` → `set_badges()`, make the template the one SEO Pro Stats now uses:
   - Row 1 (status): CI, SonarCloud (when connected), Codacy and CodeFactor (once added, as `DEVELOPMENT.md` → Services setup says), OpenSSF Scorecard (public repositories), License, Latest release (`img.shields.io/github/v/release/{owner}/{repo}`).
   - Row 2 (requirements and size): Requires WordPress, Tested up to, Requires PHP (from `readme.txt`'s header, linked to `readme.txt`), Lines of code, Dependencies.
   - Row 3: the languages chart alone.
   - No HTML comments between badges except the first line; one blank line between rows only. No "github repository" badge.
2. Let an existing plugin take the template without a rename: e.g. `scripts/rename-plugin.sh --badges-only` (or a small `scripts/readme-badges.sh` in `scripts/core-files.txt`), reading the slug from `GitHub Plugin URI` and the versions from `readme.txt`. Make it idempotent.
3. `scripts/preflight-release.sh`: warn when the badge block has a blank line or comment inside a row, an image taller than a badge outside the last row, or the requirement badges disagree with `readme.txt`.
4. `STANDARDS.md` → Structure (lines about the badges block): name the three rows, and say the block is the starter's, so other tools leave it alone.
5. Languages chart in dark mode: the chart is generated by aidevops' `loc-badge-reusable.yml`, so its colours are an aidevops change (reported there separately). Until then, keep it on its own row.

Framework side (separate, aidevops): `badges sync` and `wp_plugin_quality.py` should leave a block whose first line is `<!-- On GitHub only: the Read Me tab skips this block. scripts/rename-plugin.sh rewrites it. -->` unchanged, and the languages SVG should follow `prefers-color-scheme`.

title: Codacy settings that fit WordPress plugins: ESLint and PHPMD config files
body:
## What

Codacy analyses each plugin with the organization's default coding standard. For ESLint and PHP Mess Detector its default patterns are written for other code: on one plugin made from the starter, 3,190 ESLint findings (ES5 compatibility such as `es-x/no-modules`, `import/no-unresolved` without a TypeScript resolver, framework plugins the code does not use) and about 1,700 PHPMD findings (881 `StaticAccess`, 245 `ShortVariable`, `UnusedPrivateMethod` for methods called by name).

Codacy reads a tool's configuration file from the repository when **Code patterns → <tool> → Configuration file** is on; with a coding standard, the file controls the patterns and the standard only decides which tools run. So the fix is two core files, not a change to the organization standard (which other repositories share).

## Files

- New `.eslintrc.json` (Codacy runs ESLint 8): `eslint:recommended`; `@typescript-eslint/recommended` for `.ts`/`.tsx`; Node for `*.config.js` and `scripts/`.
- New `phpmd.xml.dist`: cleancode, codesize, design, naming and unusedcode, leaving out `StaticAccess`, `ElseExpression`, `BooleanArgumentFlag`, `MissingImport`, `ExitExpression`, `ShortVariable`, `LongVariable`, `LongClassName`, `UnusedPrivateMethod`, `UnusedFormalParameter`, and controversial.xml, each with its reason.
- `scripts/core-files.txt`, `.distignore`, `scripts/preflight-release.sh` (`DEV_FILES`): core files, out of both zips.
- `DEVELOPMENT.md` → Services setup → Codacy: turn on Configuration file for both.
- Two findings the new rules show in core files: an unused loop variable in `WPAllStars_GitHub_Updater::file_for_slug()`, and the reason for `@set_time_limit()` in `WPStarter_Feature::more_time()` for PHPMD.

## Verify

- Preview with ESLint (`ESLINT_USE_FLAT_CONFIG=false npx eslint`) and PHPMD 2.15 on a plugin made from the starter: ESLint 3,190 → 2 (an unused import and an intended control-character regex), PHPMD about 1,700 → 649 (nearly all code size and complexity).
- `scripts/lint.sh` passes; `scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline`: no development files in either zip.

title: Code smells in core files: Read Me manager's nested ternary, updater's repeated character range
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

SonarCloud code smells in two core files, found on a plugin made from the starter (wpallstars/seoprostats#160). Two exact edits; behaviour is unchanged. A third finding (`Web:S6819`, `role="group"` in `admin/includes/class-admin-page.php:166`) is marked a false positive in SonarCloud with the reason from `nav_group()`'s docblock: links, not form controls.

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `seoprostats code smells sonar cognitive complexity refactor` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 open PRs in the starter; last merges #419, #421 do not touch these lines
- [x] File refs verified: 2 refs checked at `3f3819f`, both present
- [x] Tier: `tier:simple` — exact oldString/newString for both edits, no design choice left
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — two exact edits in the brief

## What

- `admin/includes/class-readme-manager.php:99`: the nested ternary that tracks an open code fence becomes `if`/`elseif` (SonarCloud `php:S3358`).
- `includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php:617`: the redirect pattern has the `i` flag, so `A-Za-z` repeats itself; use `a-z` (SonarCloud `php:S5869`, twice on the line).

## Why

These are core files, so they change in the starter first and reach plugins through `scripts/sync-core.sh` (`STANDARDS.md` → Structure). Public plugins show their SonarCloud counts in the badges block.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:simple`

**Tier rationale:** verbatim replacements with the same behaviour, checked by `scripts/lint.sh` and the smoke test.

## PR Conventions

Leaf issue: the PR resolves this issue.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: admin/includes/class-readme-manager.php:99` — nested ternary to `if`/`elseif`
- `EDIT: includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php:617` — `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]` to `[a-z0-9_.-]` (twice)
- `EDIT: changelog.txt` — one `= Unreleased =` line
- `EDIT: README.md` — the same line in the Unreleased changelog section

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `join_wrapped_lines()` is private, called by the Read Me renderer in `admin/includes/class-readme-manager.php`; the redirect check is private in the updater's release lookup. No signature changes.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** N/A because neither line writes data: `$fence` is a local variable and `preg_match()` only reads `$location`.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `scripts/lint.sh` (PHP syntax, phpcs, PHPStan level 8); `scripts/smoke-test.sh` in CI loads the Read Me tab.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A because no settings or schema are touched (`admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php` unchanged).
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** plugins made from the starter get these files through `scripts/sync-core.sh`; nothing is built.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because no stored data changes.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `git revert` of the PR; N/A for data because nothing is stored.

### Implementation Steps

1. In `admin/includes/class-readme-manager.php`, replace

```php
                $fence   = '' === $fence ? self::fence_opens(trim($line)) : (self::fence_closes(trim($line), $fence) ? '' : $fence);
                $lines[] = $line;
```

with

```php
                if ('' === $fence) {
                    $fence = self::fence_opens(trim($line));
                } elseif (self::fence_closes(trim($line), $fence)) {
                    $fence = '';
                }
                $lines[] = $line;
```

2. In `includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php`, replace

```php
        if (preg_match('#^https://github\.com/([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)/#i', $location, $moved) && 0 !== strcasecmp($moved[1], $repo)) {
```

with

```php
        if (preg_match('#^https://github\.com/([a-z0-9_.-]+/[a-z0-9_.-]+)/#i', $location, $moved) && 0 !== strcasecmp($moved[1], $repo)) {
```

3. Add under `= Unreleased =` in `changelog.txt` and the Unreleased list in `README.md`: `Developers: two SonarCloud code smells in core files: the Read Me manager's nested ternary, and a repeated character range in Updates from GitHub's redirect check. No change in behaviour.`
4. Run `scripts/lint.sh`.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** N/A: local variables in a single request; preserved behaviour.
- **Migration/rollback:** none; a revert restores the old lines.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** same behaviour: `i` makes `a-z` match upper case, and the `if`/`elseif` leaves `$fence` unchanged when neither branch applies, as the ternary did.
- **Idempotency/retry:** unchanged; both are pure reads of their input.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** unchanged; no new error paths.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash scripts/lint.sh
```

- **Surface mapping:** `scripts/lint.sh` checks syntax, phpcs and PHPStan for both files; CI's smoke tests load the Read Me tab and the updater's hooks.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required beyond the required CI checks.

### Files Scope

- `admin/includes/class-readme-manager.php`
- `includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php`
- `changelog.txt`
- `README.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rg -n "A-Za-z0-9_.-" includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php` finds nothing on the redirect line, and `rg -n "\? '' : \\\$fence" admin/includes/class-readme-manager.php` finds nothing.
- [ ] `scripts/lint.sh` and the required CI checks pass.
- [ ] No behaviour change: code fences in a readme still render as code blocks on the Read Me tab, and a moved repository is still reported (the redirect pattern matches the same URLs).

<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: ci: choose the Actions runner from the CI_RUNNER variable
body:
## Problem

Private repositories made from this starter pay for GitHub-hosted Actions minutes, and the wpallstars organization's GitHub-hosted jobs currently fail with "recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased". The organization has self-hosted runners (runner group `hetzner`, label `4cpu-8gb`) limited to selected private repositories.

Offspring that hard-code `runs-on: [self-hosted, 4cpu-8gb]` diverge from the starter's core files (starter-sync reports them), and a public repository must never use those runners.

## Change

- Every core workflow job (except Scorecard, which runs only in public repositories) uses `runs-on: ${{ vars.CI_RUNNER || 'ubuntu-latest' }}`; reusable aidevops callers pass the same expression as `runner:`.
- The organization variable `CI_RUNNER=4cpu-8gb` is shared only with the private repositories in the `hetzner` runner group, so public repositories (the starter itself where public, and public offspring) stay GitHub-hosted with identical files.
- CI's lint job installs a pinned, checksum-verified ShellCheck 0.11.0 when the runner has another version or none (self-hosted images have none; Ubuntu's 0.9.0 reports SC2119 findings 0.11.0 does not).

## Verification

- `actionlint` clean.
- In the starter (no `CI_RUNNER`): CI jobs run on GitHub-hosted runners, or on self-hosted runners when the repository is private and receives the organization variable.
- After syncing core files into a private offspring: its CI jobs show a `hel1-01-4cpu-8gb-*` runner, and `scripts/sync-core.sh --check` reports all core files match.

title: GitHub updater: Check again did not offer a just-published release
body:
## What happened

After SEO Pro Stats 1.4.2 was published (wpallstars/seoprostats, release `v1.4.2`, about 10 minutes old), a site on 1.4.1 was not offered the update from Dashboard → Updates → Check again. It had to be installed by hand (`wp plugin install <zip> --force`). The cause is not confirmed: the install cleared the updater's cache (`wpallstars_github_releases`), so the answer the site had stored could not be read afterwards.

## Context

- The site is on shared hosting with HTTP Requests Manager in smart mode, which blocks outbound requests once a request has run 3 seconds or made 3 requests, except in cron and on `update-core.php`. On the same hosting it has earlier made WP-CLI update checks fail with `total_time_limit` recorded in `wpallstars_github_releases`.
- `includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php`: `release()` reuses a cached answer for 12 hours (`FRESH`), an hour after a failure (`RETRY`), unless `forced()` (Check again on `update-core.php`, or core's update cache cleared) and the answer is older than `RECENT`. A failure keeps the last good release, so a blocked request silently keeps offering the old one.

## Task

1. Reproduce: on a test site with a plugin made from the starter on version N, publish N+1 (or point the updater at a repository with a newer release), then press Check again. Repeat with HTTP Requests Manager smart mode on.
2. Find why Check again does not show the new release: a blocked or slow GitHub request, `forced()` not true at the time of the check, the `RECENT` window, or core's `update_plugins` transient being built before the updater's cache refreshes.
3. Fix it in the updater, and show the last failure (`failed`) on the Plugins screen or in the plugin's health check so a blocked check is visible rather than silent.

## Files

- `includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php` (`forced()`, `still_fresh()`, `release()`, `add_updates()`).
- This is a core file (`scripts/core-files.txt`): change it here, then sync it to the plugins made from the starter.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php`

## Verification

- With a newer release published, Check again offers it within one press, with and without HTTP Requests Manager smart mode.
- A blocked GitHub request is reported with its error instead of silently keeping the old release.

title: Add the banner and icon picture rules to STANDARDS.md: keep the stack, vary colours and the top tile, draw on the tile's isometric axes
body:
## What

Add the wpallstars banner and icon picture rules to the starter's shared guidance, so every plugin made from the starter keeps the same picture and varies it the same way. Learned in SEO Pro Stack (wpallstars/seoprostack#656, #660, #662), where the owner approved the result.

The rules:

1. **Keep the stack.** Every wpallstars plugin's banner and icon show the same picture: the stack of three isometric tiles under the arc of five stars, on the navy background with red and cream stripes. Never replace the stack with another picture (SEO Pro Stack #656 did, and was reverted in #660).
2. **Vary only two things:** the tiles' colours (and the matching stars and glow), and the picture on the top tile. Examples: WP Plugin Starter, all red tiles with the WordPress Plugins icon; SEO Pro Stats, rising bars; SEO Pro Stack, red, cream and blue tiles with a gold lightning bolt.
3. **Draw the top-tile picture on the tile's isometric axes.** Use the starter's face matrix, `matrix(4.95 2.871 -4.95 2.871 1214 -57.42)` (in `.wordpress-org/banner.svg` near line 106, inside the top tile's `translate(0 238)` group), with the art in a 20-unit space (0 to 20 on both axes, centre 10,10). Icon x then runs along the tile's top-right edge and icon y along its top-left edge, so straight edges are parallel to the tile's. Squashing upright art straight down (`scale(1 0.58)`) is not enough: its edges stay level and it looks wrong (SEO Pro Stack #660 → #662). Strokes scale with the matrix: about 0.35 units gives a 2 px line.
4. **Raised art** (optional, like SEO Pro Stats' bars and SEO Pro Stack's bolt): a dark shadow copy offset `translate(5 3)`, then darker side copies stepped up 1 px at a time, then the top copy with a light outline, all in tile coordinates (the `<use>` translate applies outside the face matrix).
5. Keep `banner.svg` and `icon.svg` in step (the icon is the banner's picture with no words), rebuild with `scripts/build-banner.sh`, and look at `icon-128x128.png`: the top-tile picture must still read at that size.

## How

- `STANDARDS.md`: add a bullet after "A wpallstars-branded banner keeps the starter's two words layouts" (about line 116) with rules 1 to 5, in the file's plain style. It is a core file, so plugins receive it through Starter sync.
- `.wordpress-org/banner.svg` near line 102: extend the Plugins icon comment to say this is the face matrix every plugin's top-tile picture uses. Check the stack comment near line 84 ("red, cream and blue layers") still matches the starter's own tile colours, and correct it if not.
- Reference implementation: wpallstars/seoprostack `.wordpress-org/banner.svg`, the `#bolt` polygon in `<defs>` and its `<use>` copies in the top tile group, and its `DESIGN.md` → Banner and icon.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `STANDARDS.md`
- EDIT: `.wordpress-org/banner.svg`
- EDIT: `changelog.txt`
- EDIT: `README.md`

## Verification

- `scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline --no-docker`: 0 errors (STANDARDS.md and agent-doc checks).
- If `banner.svg` changes beyond comments, run `scripts/build-banner.sh` and view `banner-772x250.png` and `icon-128x128.png`.

title: CI ShellCheck archive by runner architecture; reject misordered README badge markers
body:
## What

Two hardening gaps in core files, found by CodeRabbit on an offspring sync PR (both verified in the starter at v1.0.31). Fix them here; plugins get them through `scripts/sync-core.sh`.

1. **ShellCheck archive is x86_64 only** — `.github/workflows/ci.yml` lines 73-81 (the "pinned ShellCheck" step) always downloads `shellcheck-v$SC_VERSION.linux.x86_64.tar.gz` with one `SC_SHA256`. When `CI_RUNNER` names an ARM64 self-hosted runner, the installed binary cannot run and the lint job fails. Choose the archive and its checksum by `RUNNER_ARCH` (`X64` → `linux.x86_64`, `ARM64` → `linux.aarch64`, with the release's published SHA-256 for each), and fail with a clear message on any other architecture.
2. **Misordered badge markers can drop the rest of README.md** — `scripts/lib/plugin.sh` `plugin_badges_replace()` (around line 288) skips every line after `<!-- aidevops:badges:start -->` until the end marker. `scripts/readme-badges.sh` line 84 only checks that both markers exist, so an end marker before the start marker (or a duplicate start) makes it drop everything after the start. ### Files Scope

title: Multisite: network settings for every site (apply to all, differences, new sites) and locked choices
body:
## What

Multisite support in the core settings store and admin screen, so every plugin made from the starter can be managed for a whole network:

- **Network Admin → Settings → {Name}**: the same header, search, tab groups and cards as the site screen. Each card's switch and options save **network values** (`{prefix}_network` network option).
- **Apply to every site** (per card): the card's network values override every site's own values, and sites cannot change them. The site screen shows the card locked ("Set for every site by the network administrator", with a link to the network screen for super admins). Turning it off gives each site its own values back (sites' own values are never overwritten by it).
- **Differences**: each card says how many sites have their own different values, naming up to 10 with links to their settings, plus **Make every site the same** (a one-off copy of the card's network values into every site's own settings; sites can change them later).
- **New sites** (and sites activating the plugin for the first time) start with the network values.
- Settings changed for sites by the network run each site's `{prefix}_setting_saved` work (schedules, rules, files) on that site's next request, in its own context.
- Fields that only make sense per site are never set for the network: `media` fields, `hidden` wiring, and fields with `'network' => false` in the schema.
- `multi` fields accept `'locked'` (values or a callable): those choices show ticked and cannot be unticked, and are not stored (the feature treats them as always chosen). First use: super admins in SEO Pro Stack's developer list.

## Why

SEO Pro Stack (wpallstars/seoprostack) needs a network settings panel that applies to every site, shows sites that differ, and keeps site administrators from switching off what the network sets. The store and screen are core files (`STANDARDS.md` → Structure), so this lands in the starter first and reaches each plugin with `scripts/sync-core.sh`.

## How

Files (core, `scripts/core-files.txt`):

- NEW `includes/class-wpstarter-network-settings.php` (`WPStarter_Network_Settings`): network option, values, applied cards, per-site field rules, differences (one indexed `option_name` query per site, up to 500 sites), Make every site the same, per-site sync on `wp_loaded` (network `version` and `touched` key versions against the site's `{prefix}_network_seen`), seed values for first installs, AJAX actions `{prefix}_network_apply` and `{prefix}_network_copy`.
- EDIT `includes/class-wpstarter-settings.php`: `all()` overlays applied network values; `own()` without them; `set()` refuses applied keys; `sanitize_all()` stores own values only; `maybe_migrate()` seeds first installs; `ajax_save()` saves network values when `network=1` (`manage_network_options`); `sanitize_multi()` drops locked values.
- EDIT `includes/class-wpstarter.php`: load the new class.
- NEW `admin/includes/class-network-manager.php`: network cards (switch, Apply to every site, differences, options without the site-only `{prefix}_setting_panel` tools).
- EDIT `admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php`, `class-settings-manager.php`, `admin/settings.php`, `admin/js/wpstarter-admin.js`, `admin/css/wpstarter-admin.css`: network menu, URLs, tabs (`'network' => true` for plugin tabs that work there), locked cards and choices, network saves.
- Docs: `STANDARDS.md` (multisite rules), `README.md` (field keys `network`, `locked`; Multisite section), `changelog.txt`, `scripts/core-files.txt`, `uninstall.php` (network option and per-site seen option).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Single sites: no change in behaviour, markup or queries (no network option read).
- [ ] Network screen saves network values only; a site admin's AJAX save of an applied key fails with a clear message; super admins see the lock and a link.
- [ ] Applying a card overrides every site's effective value; switching it off restores each site's own value.
- [ ] Differences list sites whose own values differ; Make every site the same copies the values and the list then says every site is the same.
- [ ] A new site gets the network values; its `{prefix}_setting_saved` work runs on its next request.
- [ ] Locked choices render ticked and disabled and are not stored.
- [ ] `scripts/lint.sh` passes; smoke test passes.

## Verification

Throwaway Docker multisite (`wordpress:php8.3-apache`, `wp core multisite-install`) with SEO Pro Stack synced from this branch (`scripts/sync-core.sh --from <starter worktree>`): exercise each criterion in the browser and with WP-CLI; debug log clean. `scripts/lint.sh`; `scripts/smoke-test.sh`.

title: Settings screen: browser title shows the screen's name followed by the tab
body:
## What

The browser tab title of the settings screen names only the screen ("WP Plugin Starter ‹ Site — WordPress"), whatever tab is open, so several open tabs of the screen look the same and history entries cannot be told apart. Show the screen's name followed by the tab: "WP Plugin Starter: Read Me ‹ Site — WordPress" (in the plugin's own menu: "WP Plugin Starter settings: General ‹ …"). Search results show "…: Search results".

Tabs of one group switch without a reload (`admin/js/wpstarter-admin.js` → `Tabs.show()`), so the script must update `document.title` too, including on Back/Forward.

The plugin's own screens with sections (`render_header()` + `.wps-nav`) should be able to do the same with one call.

### Approach

- `admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php`: on `load-{hook}` add an `admin_title` filter that puts the active tab's label after core's `$title` (replace its first occurrence, so core's site name, Network Admin and Recovery Mode parts stay). Public helper `title_section($label)` for the plugin's own screens (call on their `load-{hook}`); one translatable format (`%1$s: %2$s`).
- Pass the full title of each tab drawn on the page to the script (`wpstarterAdmin.titles`), and swap it in `document.title` in `Tabs.show()`.
- No `$GLOBALS['title']` override (PHPCS `WordPress.WP.GlobalVariablesOverride`).
- Docs: `STANDARDS.md` → Structure (settings screen bullet), `README.md` → Developers, changelog (`README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php`
- EDIT: `admin/js/wpstarter-admin.js`
- EDIT: `STANDARDS.md`
- EDIT: `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`

All but the last three are core files: every plugin made from the starter picks the change up with `scripts/sync-core.sh` (its `starter-sync` issue).

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` passes.
- On a test site: Settings → WP Plugin Starter shows "WP Plugin Starter: General ‹ {site} — WordPress"; `&tab=readme` shows "…: Read Me ‹ …"; a search shows "…: Search results ‹ …".
- Switching tabs of the same group without a reload changes the title; Back restores the previous tab's title.
- `debug.log` has no new messages.

title: t9: Admin colour mode (Light / Dark / System) in the starter, shared with every offspring plugin
body:
## Task


Every plugin made from the starter gets a Light / Dark / System colour mode on its own admin screens, kept in step with the other wpallstars plugins:

- A colour mode button in the screen header (`WPStarter_Admin_Page::header()`), right of Buy me a coffee. It opens a menu with three choices that works with the keyboard and screen readers.
- The choice is saved per person in user meta: the shared `wpallstars_admin_theme` first, then the plugin's own `{prefix}_admin_theme`. Saving is AJAX with a nonce and the `manage_options` capability (network screens: `manage_network_options`).
- A `<head>` script sets `{css}-theme-{mode}` and, when dark, `{css}-dark` on `<html>` before the first paint (System follows `prefers-color-scheme` live).
- Dark styles are scoped to `html.{css}-dark` and cover the header, the tabs, the cards and the WordPress classic elements on the plugin's screens.
- It takes part in the `wpallstars_admin_theme_participants` filter, so SEO Pro Stack shows its admin bar icon. After a successful save it sends the `wpallstars-admin-theme` document event, and it listens for that event so the header button and SEO Pro Stack's admin bar icon follow each other.
- It returns false from `seoprostack_admin_dark_screen` on its own screens, so SEO Pro Stack's whole-admin dark rules never mix with the plugin's own.
- The screens it covers: the settings screen (`WPStarter_Admin_Manager::hook()`), the network settings screen (`WPStarter_Network_Manager::hook()`) and every own screen that calls `WPStarter_Admin_Manager::render_header()`.
- The new files are core files (`scripts/core-files.txt`), so offspring get them through `scripts/sync-core.sh`.

## Done when

- [ ] The settings screen, the network settings screen and render_header() screens have a working Light / Dark / System button that saves to `wpallstars_admin_theme` and syncs with SEO Pro Stack's admin bar icon both ways.
- [ ] The three new files are core files.
- [ ] Regression: Light mode and screens that are not the plugin's own must not change; every dark selector is behind `html.wps-dark`, and SEO Pro Stack's dark stylesheet never loads on the plugin's screens.
- [ ] `scripts/lint.sh php js shell phpcs phpstan` passes and CI is green.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Progressive Context Plan

- **Read first:** wpallstars/seoprodirectory at `main` (16543fd): `includes/admin/class-seoprodirectory-admin-theme.php` (190 lines), `admin/js/seoprodirectory-theme.js` (308), `admin/css/seoprodirectory-theme.css` (441). Read them with `gh api repos/wpallstars/seoprodirectory/contents/<path>`. They map to the starter's names with `seoprodirectory`→`wpstarter`, `SEOProDirectory`→`WPStarter`, `SEOPRODIRECTORY`→`WPSTARTER`, `spd`→`wps`.
- **Load only if:** System mode or the event sync misbehaves: SEO Pro Stats' `includes/admin/class-seoprostats-admin-theme.php` and `admin/js/seoprostats-theme.js`. They are the original pattern, with extra Light-mode accent capping that is out of scope here.
- **Why:** the shared contract (meta keys, event name, participants filter, Stack opt-out filter) must stay identical across plugins.
- **Stop when:** the PHP hooks, the JS event contract and the CSS sections are mapped to the starter's screens.
- **For UI/UX tasks:** `STYLING.md` (admin styling rules) and `STANDARDS.md` → front-end styling and dark mode. The palette is SPD's dark tokens (#1d2327 surfaces, #f0f0f1 text), kept consistent with SEO Pro Stats.

### Files to Modify

- `NEW: admin/includes/class-admin-theme.php` — class `WPStarter_Admin_Theme`, ported from SPD's class. `is_screen()` must accept the settings hook, the network settings hook and screens that render the header (render_header can set a static flag the class reads, or the class can expose `WPStarter_Admin_Theme::screens()` for plugins to extend through a `wpstarter_admin_theme_screens` filter).
- `NEW: admin/css/wpstarter-theme.css` — ported from SPD's CSS; selectors `.wps-*` behind `html.wps-dark`.
- `NEW: admin/js/wpstarter-theme.js` — ported from SPD's JS.
- `EDIT: admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php:64` — call `WPStarter_Admin_Theme::init()` from `init()` (require the file where the manager loads its siblings).
- `EDIT: admin/includes/class-admin-page.php:83` — optional: render the button's container in `header_links()` so the JS doesn't shift the layout (SPD inserts it from JS).
- `EDIT: scripts/core-files.txt` — add the three new files.
- `EDIT: uninstall.php` — delete `{prefix}_admin_theme`, and `wpallstars_admin_theme` only when no other wpallstars plugin is installed (SPD's `uninstall.php:79-83` pattern; also check for each other plugin's main file, or use a single helper `WPStarter_Admin_Theme::uninstall()` that the plugin's uninstall.php calls).
- `EDIT: STANDARDS.md` — a short "Admin colour mode" rule: the shared meta, event and filters; every plugin's uninstall.php calls the helper; own screens get it by calling render_header().
- `EDIT: STYLING.md` — the dark palette for admin screens.
- `EDIT: README.md`, `changelog.txt` — describe the feature (Unreleased).

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `WPStarter_Admin_Manager::init()` loads it. The `<head>` script, the enqueue and the AJAX save are in the new class. SEO Pro Stack reads `wpallstars_admin_theme_participants` and `seoprostack_admin_dark_screen` (`seoprostack/includes/admin/class-seoprostack-admin-theme.php:185,209`). SEO Pro Stats and SEO Pro Stack listen for `wpallstars-admin-theme`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** the AJAX save writes user meta `wpallstars_admin_theme` and `wpstarter_admin_theme`. Nothing else writes them in the starter (`rg wpallstars_admin_theme` at HEAD: no hits).
- **Existing verification/tests:** `scripts/lint.sh` (php js shell phpcs phpstan), `scripts/smoke-test.sh`, `scripts/preview-site.sh`, CI `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. There are no unit tests for admin screens.
- **Schemas/config:** `scripts/core-files.txt`. `phpstan` config may need the new class path if it scans by list.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** offspring copies via `scripts/sync-core.sh` (run in each plugin later, out of scope here).
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because the meta keys are the ones SPD and Stats already write (`wpallstars_admin_theme`, `{prefix}_admin_theme`), so existing values are read as they are.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `uninstall.php` deletes the meta; reverting the PR removes the three files, the `core-files.txt` lines and the init call.

### Implementation Steps

1. Port the three SPD files with the token rename; replace `SEOProDirectory_Admin_Manager::hook()` checks with the three screen kinds above. On network screens, check `manage_network_options`.
2. Load from `WPStarter_Admin_Manager::init()`. Add the files to `scripts/core-files.txt`.
3. Add the uninstall cleanup and the STANDARDS.md / STYLING.md / README.md / changelog.txt text.
4. `scripts/lint.sh php js shell phpcs phpstan`, then check it in a browser (below).

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** two tabs saving at once: last write wins, same as SPD and Stats; the event updates the other tab only on its next load (accepted).
- **Migration/rollback:** none; meta keys unchanged.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** offspring that already have their own copy (seoprostats, seoprodirectory) would load two classes after `sync-core.sh`. The class names differ (`SEOProDirectory_Admin_Theme` vs the synced core class), so both would print a button. The rollout follow-ups below must delete the private copies in the same PR as the sync.
- **Idempotency/retry:** saving the same mode twice is harmless.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** the event is sent only after a successful save, so a failed save never moves SEO Pro Stack's icon (SPD behaviour; keep it).

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash scripts/lint.sh php js shell phpcs phpstan
bash scripts/smoke-test.sh
# Runtime: a site with the starter plus SEO Pro Stack active (scripts/preview-site.sh), Dark mode:
#  - <html> has wps-theme-dark wps-dark before <body> is parsed (no flash)
#  - header, tabs and cards are dark; header button -> Light saves and SEO Pro Stack's admin bar icon follows; admin bar -> Dark and the button follows
#  - System follows prefers-color-scheme live; reload keeps the choice
#  - SEO Pro Stack adds no sps-dark class or its stylesheet on the starter's screens
#  - the network settings screen (multisite) behaves the same
```

- **Surface mapping:** lint covers the PHP, JS and core-file list. The browser checks cover the head script, the AJAX save, the event sync and the Stack opt-out.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required beyond the repo's own lint and smoke test.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused functional verification passes: `scripts/lint.sh php js phpcs phpstan`
- [ ] WIP commit created before broad gates: `wip: admin colour mode core files`
- [ ] Evidence-triggered broad verification then run: not required — no shared tooling changes

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** starter repo only. Do not change offspring repos in this PR, and do not change SEO Pro Stack's whole-admin dark mode (tracked in wpallstars/seoprostack).

**AI brief owner:** the interactive session that filed this issue (marcusquinn).

- `admin/includes/class-admin-theme.php`
- `admin/css/wpstarter-theme.css`
- `admin/js/wpstarter-theme.js`
- `admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php`

- `STYLING.md`
- `README.md`
- `changelog.txt`
- `phpstan.neon.dist`

Integration scope correction: DESIGN.md records the introduced admin palette and responsive menu conventions; readme.txt receives the short user-facing feature line required by STANDARDS.md. The issue author is the repository owner and the current worker retains ownership. Collision discovery found no overlapping open PR. Verification: existing lint, release preflight and browser mode checks. No offspring or other hard boundary changes.

title: Multisite: network classes over PHP Mess Detector's complexity limits (Codacy fails in plugins)
body:
## What

Plugins made from the starter whose Codacy runs PHP Mess Detector with `phpmd.xml.dist` (`rulesets/codesize.xml`) fail that check on the new multisite core files. SEO Pro Stack's pull request https://github.com/wpallstars/seoprostack/pull/713 shows four new issues, and PHPMD 2.15.0 with `phpmd.xml.dist` reports the same four in the starter at 80cc6d9:

- `includes/class-wpstarter-network-sites.php`: `WPStarter_Network_Sites` has an overall complexity of 72 (limit 50).
- `includes/class-wpstarter-network-sites.php`: `differences()` has a cyclomatic complexity of 10 (limit 10).
- `includes/class-wpstarter-network-settings.php`: `WPStarter_Network_Settings` 51.
- `admin/includes/class-network-manager.php`: `WPStarter_Network_Manager` 52.

Every earlier pull request in that plugin passed Codacy, so they are fixed in the code, and in the starter first (`STANDARDS.md` → Structure).

## How

- Move the network screen's part of `WPStarter_Network_Sites` (`differences()`, `copy()`, `forget()`, `MAX_SITES` and their helpers) to a new core file, `includes/class-wpstarter-network-differences.php` (`WPStarter_Network_Differences`). `WPStarter_Network_Sites` keeps each site's part (`seed()`, `sync()`, `syncing()`, the `wpstarter_network_seen` record and `flush_site_cache()`), so `{Prefix}_Network_Sites::syncing()` in `STANDARDS.md` → Multisite stays as it is.
- `differences()`: a helper lists the cards the network screen shows.
- `WPStarter_Network_Settings`: `eligible()` and `value()` read optional keys with `??` (same results).
- `WPStarter_Network_Manager`: the screen's hook suffix with a `(string)` cast, and the card a setting is on from a new `WPStarter_Settings::card_of()`, next to `children_of()`.
- Name the new file in `scripts/core-files.txt`, `includes/class-wpstarter.php`, `STANDARDS.md` (Structure, Multisite) and the Unreleased notes in `README.md` and `changelog.txt`.

Behaviour, markup, queries and options stay as they are.

## Verification

- PHPMD 2.15 with `phpmd.xml.dist` reports none of the four (`WPStarter_Settings` keeps the size findings it already has on `main`).
- `scripts/lint.sh` and `scripts/smoke-test.sh` pass.
- On a test network: the network screen still names the sites that differ, Make every site the same still copies a card's values, and Apply to every site still locks the card on each site.
- `scripts/sync-core.sh` in SEO Pro Stack, then its pull request's Codacy check passes.
