title: Preview site browser checks: sign in, check, sign out and read new debug log lines (scripts/preview-browser.sh)
body:
## What

A core script that lets agents, including headless workers, check admin screens on the shared preview site in a browser as an administrator, and read the debug log lines a check added. Every plugin made from the starter asks for this check (`DEVELOPMENT.md` → Workflow step 5, `STANDARDS.md` → Testing), but there is no supported way to sign in, so each session improvises.

## Why (evidence)

- SEO Pro Stack GH#707 (wpallstars/seoprostack#707): the headless worker finished the code and opened the PR, then stopped at the preview-site check. It needed to read Local's run folder (`~/Library/Application Support/Local/…`) for the database socket, and the worker permission boundary refused that, so the issue waited for a maintainer.
- The interactive session that finished it wrote throwaway scripts: PHP booting `wp-load.php` with the site's MySQL socket, creating a `WP_Session_Tokens` session for an administrator and `wp_generate_auth_cookie()` cookies; Playwright adding those cookies in-process, checking titles, then destroying the session. Homebrew PHP's default 128 MB `memory_limit` could not boot a site with many plugins (fatal in WooCommerce's autoloader), and those fatals went into the site's debug log.
- WP-CLI is not always installed, and the site's own PHP lives inside Local's folders.

A script run through Bash avoids file-tool permission prompts, as `scripts/preview-site.sh` already writes to the site outside the repository.

## How

New core script `scripts/preview-browser.sh` (add to `scripts/core-files.txt`; it stays out of both zips like the other scripts):

1. **Site:** resolve it as `scripts/preview-site.sh` does (argument, `<PREFIX>_PREVIEW_SITE`, then the remembered `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/{slug}-preview-site`). Move `resolve_site()` into `scripts/lib/plugin.sh` so both scripts share it.
2. **PHP:** run `php` with `-d memory_limit=1024M`. For a Local site, find its MySQL socket by matching the site folder (`<path>/app/public`) against `path` in `~/Library/Application Support/Local/sites.json`, then use `run/<id>/mysql/mysqld.sock` as `mysqli.default_socket`. `<PREFIX>_PREVIEW_PHP_ARGS` overrides this for other local hosts. Never print or store the database password from `sites.json`.
3. **`login [--user <id|login>]`:** create a one-hour session for that user (default: the first administrator) and write a Playwright `storageState` JSON (auth or secure_auth cookie for `ADMIN_COOKIE_PATH`, logged_in cookie for `COOKIEPATH`, domain from `admin_url()`, plus the session token for logout) to a new mode-600 file under `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}`. Print only the file path, the admin URL and the expiry, never cookie values.
4. **`logout <state-file>`:** destroy that session token and delete the file.
5. **`log-mark` / `log-since <mark> [--all]`:** read `WP_DEBUG_LOG`'s path from WordPress, print a mark (line count), then the lines added since it, by default only those naming the plugin's slug or folder.
6. **Docs:** `DEVELOPMENT.md` → Preview site: a short "Checking screens in a browser" paragraph with the login → check → logout → log-since sequence and a minimal Playwright example using `storageState`. Agents must log out when done. Changelog: a "Developers:" line.

Out of scope: page caching or front-end visitor checks; installing WP-CLI or Playwright.

## Verification

- On a plugin's preview site: `scripts/preview-browser.sh login` prints a path; the file is mode 600; stdout and stderr hold no cookie values.
- Playwright with that `storageState` opens the settings screen (`options-general.php?page={slug}`) signed in. After `logout`, the same request redirects to `wp-login.php`, and the file is gone.
- `log-mark`, then a page load, then `log-since` shows only lines written after the mark. No PHP fatals from the script itself (memory limit raised).
- Works from a linked worktree and from a headless worker without file-tool reads outside the repository.
- `scripts/lint.sh` passes (ShellCheck clean).

### Files Scope

- NEW: `scripts/preview-browser.sh`
- EDIT: `scripts/lib/plugin.sh` (shared `resolve_site()`)
- EDIT: `scripts/preview-site.sh` (use the shared helper)
- EDIT: `scripts/core-files.txt`
- EDIT: `DEVELOPMENT.md`
- EDIT: `changelog.txt`, `README.md` (Developers line)

title: Multisite: settings screen methods and WPStarter_Settings over PHP Mess Detector's limits
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `PHPMD complexity seoprostack starter refactor Codacy` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 2 commits / 0 merged PRs / 1 open PR touch target files in last 48h — 80cc6d9 (GH#452, merged) and 248a212 (#458, GH#457, open: this issue waits for it)
- [x] File refs verified: 27 file:line refs checked at 248a212 (#458's head), all present
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — known extract-method pattern on verified targets; the worker chooses helper boundaries
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — #458 still changes the same files; a seed now would conflict

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-12
- **Created by:** ai-interactive, while finishing SEO Pro Stack's multisite pull request (https://github.com/wpallstars/seoprostack/pull/713, GH#694)
- **Blocked by:** #457 (GitHub relationship), `blocked-by:#457`. Its pull request #458 changes `includes/class-wpstarter-settings.php`, `scripts/core-files.txt`, `includes/class-wpstarter.php`, `STANDARDS.md` and the Unreleased notes; start after it merges.
- **Conversation context:** #457 fixed the four PHP Mess Detector findings Codacy reported on the network classes. Comparing PHPMD's full reports for SEO Pro Stack's pull request and its `main` found seven more in core files, all added by GH#452.

## What

PHP Mess Detector 2.15.0 with `phpmd.xml.dist` reports seven findings that the multisite work (GH#452, 80cc6d9) added to core files. At 6962e6a, just before it, it reports none of them. Line numbers are at 248a212 (#458), where a run with an empty cache (Worker Quick-Start) reports all seven:

| Where | Finding | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| `admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php:138` | `get_tabs()`: cyclomatic complexity 11 | 10 |
| `admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php:201` | `render_card()`: cyclomatic complexity 13, NPath 256 | 10, 200 |
| `admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php:463` | `render_replaces()`: cyclomatic complexity 10 | 10 |
| `admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php:546` | `render_field()`: cyclomatic complexity 11 | 10 |
| `admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php:636` | `render_multi()`: cyclomatic complexity 10 | 10 |
| `includes/class-wpstarter-settings.php:28` | `WPStarter_Settings`: 1,079 lines | 1,000 |

Done means PHPMD reports none of the seven, and the settings screen and the network screen show exactly the same HTML as before.

## Why

Every plugin made from the starter copies these core files, and Codacy checks them with `phpmd.xml.dist`. Codacy does not report these seven today (SEO Pro Stack's pull request passes with them), so nothing fails; this is size debt that GH#452 added. The class-level findings that were already on `main` before GH#452 stay, and are not part of this: `WPStarter_Settings` complexity and method counts, and `WPStarter_Settings_Manager` and `WPStarter_Admin_Manager` complexity.

## How (Approach)

### Progressive Context Plan

- **Read first:** the six methods named in What, and `includes/class-wpstarter-settings.php:48-59` and `:673-966` (sanitizers and parsers).
- **Load only if:** a helper boundary is unclear: the earlier splits 99a9144 (GH#285, `render_field()` into one method per control), 689ec51 (GH#295, settings store into small sanitizers) and f69b139 (GH#311, complex methods split).
- **Why:** the same extract-method pattern, with HTML, values, hooks and filters unchanged.
- **Stop when:** each method's new helper is chosen and the HTML check below is ready.

### Worker Quick-Start

- PHPMD is not in `composer.json`. Install it in a temporary folder outside the repository (`PHPMD_DIR` below) with `composer require --working-dir="$PHPMD_DIR" phpmd/phpmd:2.15.0`, then run it from the repository as in Verification Before Dispatch. `-d 'error_reporting=E_ALL & ~E_DEPRECATED'` hides PHPMD 2.15's own deprecation notices on new PHP versions.
- Give every PHPMD run an empty cache: `env HOME="$(mktemp -d)"` before `php`, as in Verification Before Dispatch. PDepend (PHPMD 2.15.0 runs PDepend 2.16.2) keeps its metrics in `~/.pdepend` per list of files analysed, under IDs made from file paths (`vendor/pdepend/pdepend/src/main/php/PDepend/Engine.php`, `createAnalyzers()`). Once another run (of one file, say) has parsed a changed file, a later run with an earlier list reports that file's old numbers. While this brief was written, a run gave the numbers from before a commit, showing findings that were already fixed.
- PDepend counts the `&&`, `||` and `?:` inside a closure in the method around it, and does not count `??` (#457 used `??` to bring `WPStarter_Network_Settings` under its limit).
- A private static method works as a callback from inside its class (`array(__CLASS__, 'name')`), as `WPStarter_Settings::parse_times()` passes `time_of()` to `array_map()`. `phpmd.xml.dist` leaves out UnusedPrivateMethod for this reason.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php:138` — `get_tabs()`: the `array_filter()` callback at its end (the user can use the tab, and on the network screen the tab has `'network' => true`) becomes a private static method passed as `array(__CLASS__, '…')`.
- `EDIT: admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php:201` — `render_card()`: GH#452 added the `$network` and `$locked` branches. Move the header's text block (title row, description, `render_replaces()` and the locked note) into a private helper, then anything else needed for under 10 and NPath under 200.
- `EDIT: admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php:463` — `render_replaces()`: GH#452 added two `$network ?` ternaries for the plugin lists. One helper that returns both lists for the screen, or the per-plugin loop in a helper, brings it under 10.
- `EDIT: admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php:546` — `render_field()`: move the description and tokens paragraph into a private helper. `isset($field['description']) ? $field['description'] : ''` can read `$field['description'] ?? ''`.
- `EDIT: admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php:636` — `render_multi()`: build the list of choices (saved items not registered now, and locked choices) in a helper.
- `NEW: includes/class-wpstarter-sanitizer.php` — `WPStarter_Sanitizer`, the field-type sanitizers moved from `WPStarter_Settings`: the `SANITIZERS` map (lines 48-59), and lines 673-877: `sanitize_value()`'s body as a public `sanitize($value, array $field)`, `default_of()`, `to_text()`, and `sanitize_bool()` to `sanitize_text()`. Model the file header (SPDX lines, `@package`, ABSPATH guard) on `includes/class-wpstarter-network-differences.php`. The sanitizers keep calling `WPStarter_Settings::options_for()`, `locked_values()`, `parse_domains()` and `parse_times()`, which are public.
- `EDIT: includes/class-wpstarter-settings.php` — `sanitize_value()` becomes a one-line call to `WPStarter_Sanitizer::sanitize()`. Keep `sanitize_value()`, `parse_domains()`, `host_matches()` and `parse_times()` public with the same signatures and results: plugins call them (SEO Pro Stack from `includes/class-seoprostack-setup.php`, `class-seoprostack-starters.php`, and its iframe block, auto upload and post scheduler features). The parsers stay here. Together with the sanitizers, one class would be over the class complexity limit of 50 (PDepend ccn2: sanitizers 40, parsers 24). The parsers use `to_text()`: call the new class's (public) one.
- `EDIT: includes/class-wpstarter.php:39` — `require_once` the new file next to `class-wpstarter-settings.php`.
- `EDIT: scripts/core-files.txt` — list the new file, so `scripts/sync-core.sh` copies it with the rest.
- `EDIT: STANDARDS.md:25-32` — name the new file in Structure's core files list.
- `EDIT: README.md:150` and `changelog.txt:5` — a Developers line under Unreleased, as #457's: the new core file, plus methods split with HTML, values, hooks and filters unchanged.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `WPStarter_Settings::sanitize_value()` is called by `includes/class-wpstarter-settings.php:378` (`set()`) and `:998` (`sanitize_all()`), `includes/class-wpstarter-network-settings.php:225` and `includes/class-wpstarter-feature.php:176`, and by plugins (above). `render_card()` is called at `admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php:125` and `:162`, `render_field()` at `:333` and `:344`, `render_replaces()` at `:242`. `get_tabs()` is called in `admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php` (`:215`, `:233`, `:405`, `:468`) and `admin/includes/class-admin-page.php:144`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** none new. The sanitizers return values; `set()`, `sanitize_all()` and the network save store them as before.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `scripts/lint.sh` (PHPCS, PHPStan level 8), `scripts/smoke-test.sh` (loads the admin screens with every feature on and fails on any PHP message), CI's Plugin Check. The repository has no unit tests.
- **Schemas/config:** no schema keys, options or `phpmd.xml.dist` changes.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** plugins made from the starter get core files with `scripts/sync-core.sh` (the Starter sync workflow); the new file reaches them only when it is in `scripts/core-files.txt`.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none, because no option key or value changes: `wpstarter_options` and the migrations in `WPStarter_Settings::maybe_migrate()` stay as they are.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `git revert` of the merged change is the whole rollback, because nothing new is stored (no options, transients, cron events or files).

### Implementation Steps

1. Before the first edit, record the HTML of every tab on a throwaway site (`STANDARDS.md` → Testing, step 4), on a single site and, after `wp core multisite-convert`, on the network screen, with the script below. Keep the output.
2. Split the five methods and `get_tabs()` as above. Run PHPMD after each one.
3. Move the sanitizers into `WPStarter_Sanitizer`, then wire up `includes/class-wpstarter.php`, `scripts/core-files.txt`, `STANDARDS.md` and the notes.
4. Run the HTML script again on the same site, in the same session (nonces change every 12 hours). Every tab's hash must match.

```php
<?php
// wp eval-file render-tabs.php [network]: one "tab md5 bytes" line per settings-screen tab.
$network = isset($args[0]) && 'network' === $args[0];
// WP-CLI is not the admin, so the plugin has not loaded its admin classes.
require_once ABSPATH . 'wp-admin/includes/admin.php';
require_once WPSTARTER_DIR . 'admin/settings.php';
wp_set_current_user(1);
// is_network_admin() reads the current screen; a "-network" screen is in the network admin.
set_current_screen('settings_page_' . WPStarter_Admin_Manager::PAGE . ($network ? '-network' : ''));
foreach (WPStarter_Admin_Manager::get_tabs() as $slug => $tab) {
    ob_start();
    call_user_func($tab['render']);
    $html = (string) ob_get_clean();
    printf("%-14s %s %d\n", $slug, md5($html), strlen($html));
}
```

This script was checked in SEO Pro Stack (same core code, `SEOProStack_` prefix): two runs a minute apart gave the same hashes for all 15 site tabs and 13 network tabs.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** none added. The save lock in `set()` and the network save are not touched.
- **Migration/rollback:** no stored data changes, so a revert is the whole rollback.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** plugin code calling `{Prefix}_Settings::sanitize_value()`, `parse_domains()`, `host_matches()` or `parse_times()` keeps working through the kept public methods. A plugin that syncs `class-{prefix}-settings.php` without the new file would stop with a fatal error, so `scripts/core-files.txt` must list it (sync-core copies the listed files together).
- **Idempotency/retry:** sanitizers must stay idempotent: `update_option()` runs `sanitize_all()` again on sanitized values. Move the code; do not change it.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** no writes or network calls are added.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
composer require --working-dir="$PHPMD_DIR" phpmd/phpmd:2.15.0
env HOME="$(mktemp -d)" php -d 'error_reporting=E_ALL & ~E_DEPRECATED' "$PHPMD_DIR/vendor/bin/phpmd" admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php,admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php,includes/class-wpstarter-settings.php,includes/class-wpstarter-sanitizer.php text phpmd.xml.dist
bash scripts/lint.sh
bash scripts/smoke-test.sh
wp --url="$SITE_URL" eval-file render-tabs.php
wp --url="$NETWORK_MAIN_SITE_URL" eval-file render-tabs.php network
```

- **Surface mapping:** PHPMD proves the seven findings are gone and that the new class adds none. `scripts/lint.sh` proves PHPCS and PHPStan level 8 are clean in every changed file. `scripts/smoke-test.sh` switches every feature on through `{Prefix}_Settings::set()`, which runs `sanitize_value()` and then `sanitize_all()` on every stored field, and loads the site and admin screens without PHP messages. The render script proves the markup is unchanged on both screens.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required; the changes stay inside the core files listed.

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** no change to HTML, stored values, hooks, filters, public method signatures or `phpmd.xml.dist`. The class-level findings that were on `main` before GH#452 stay as they are.

**AI brief owner:** the interactive session that filed this issue (marcusquinn).

**Recovery:** preserve the current PR and use the structured runtime request and Pulse intake in `reference/worker-discipline.md` when local recovery is unsafe.

### Files Scope

- `admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php`
- `admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php`
- `includes/class-wpstarter-settings.php`
- `includes/class-wpstarter-sanitizer.php`
- `includes/class-wpstarter.php`
- `scripts/core-files.txt`
- `STANDARDS.md`
- `README.md`
- `changelog.txt`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] PHPMD 2.15.0 with `phpmd.xml.dist` reports none of the seven findings in What, and nothing for `includes/class-wpstarter-sanitizer.php`.
- [ ] Regression guarantee: every tab's HTML hash from the render script is the same before and after, on a single site and on the network screen, so no markup changes.
- [ ] `WPStarter_Settings::sanitize_value()`, `parse_domains()`, `host_matches()` and `parse_times()` stay public with the same signatures and results, so plugins calling them do not change.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "public static function (sanitize_value|parse_domains|host_matches|parse_times)\\("
    path: "includes/class-wpstarter-settings.php"
  ```

- [ ] The new core file is listed for plugins made from the starter.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "includes/class-wpstarter-sanitizer.php"
    path: "scripts/core-files.txt"
  ```

- [ ] `bash scripts/lint.sh` and `bash scripts/smoke-test.sh` pass.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** #457 (pull request #458).
- **Blocks:** nothing. SEO Pro Stack and other plugins made from the starter pick it up with their next starter sync.

title: sync-core.sh: never undo a newer starter change or discard a plugin's own change
body:
## What

`scripts/sync-core.sh` replaces every core file that differs from the starter at `--ref`, whatever the reason it differs. Two of those reasons lose work:

- **Newer than the ref.** The plugin already has a later starter version of the file. Syncing from an older ref (a release tag, say) puts the old version back and undoes a starter improvement.
- **Changed only in the plugin.** The plugin changed a core file outside its `{css}-own` blocks. Syncing overwrites that change before it reaches the starter.

`sync-core.sh` should tell these apart from a file that is simply behind, and write nothing that would lose either kind of change.

## Why

Core files have to keep flowing both ways: starter improvements out to every plugin, and what a plugin learns back into the starter (`STANDARDS.md` → Structure). Today nothing stops a sync going backwards or discarding a plugin's change.

Seen in SEO Pro Stats: wpallstars/seoprostats#286 synced the shared updater 1.6.2 from the starter's `main` (after #462), while that plugin's open core-sync task syncs from `v1.0.34`, which has updater 1.6.1. Following that task as written would quietly undo #462 there. It is caught only by a comment on the task (wpallstars/seoprostats#274).

**Not in scope: syncing only some core files.** A partial sync leaves a plugin with core files from different starter versions. That is exactly the drift this issue guards against, so `sync-core.sh` keeps syncing every core file in one run.

## How

For each core file that differs, look at the starter checkout's history for that path. Compare the plugin's file with each starter version, mapped to this plugin's names and with its own blocks kept, the same way `sync_file` maps the file at `--ref`:

| Class | The plugin's file equals | Sync |
|---|---|---|
| behind | the starter's file at a commit `--ref` contains | updates it, as today |
| newer | the starter's file at a commit `--ref` does not contain (later on `main`, or another branch) | stops |
| changed here | no starter version | stops |
| missing | (absent) | adds it, as today |

- **`--check`:** keep today's lines exactly (`  differs  <path>`, `  missing  <path>`, `  mode     <path> (executable bit)`) and keep the summary as the last line. Each plugin's own copy of `.github/workflows/starter-sync.yml` may be older than the starter's, and it runs the starter's newest `sync-core.sh --check`, reading those lines with `sed -nE 's/^  (differs|missing)  (.*)$/\1 \2/p'` and the summary with `tail -n 1`. Put the class on its own indented line under each file, saying what to do. The old pattern must skip that line.
- **Sync:** before writing anything (the existing validate-first pass, `sync_file ... 2`), stop with exit 2 and write nothing if any file is **newer** or **changed here**. List each one with what to do:
  - **newer:** sync from a starter ref that contains it: the starter's `main` (what the weekly Starter sync checks against), or a later tag.
  - **changed here:** take the change to the starter first (a pull request, or an issue there with the plugin's case), or move plugin-only lines into `{css}-own` blocks. Then run again with `--discard-local`, a new option that replaces changed-here files once their change is safe. There is no option to go backwards; the fix for newer files is always a newer ref.
- **History not available** (a shallow clone of the starter): `--check` still lists the files, with the class "unknown (shallow starter clone)", and exits as today. A sync stops and says to run `git -C <starter> fetch --unshallow`.
- **`starter-sync.yml`:** check out the starter with `fetch-depth: 0` so the weekly check can classify files, and show each file's class in the issue body. Step 3 of the issue's "How" already says a plugin-only change goes to the starter first; point it at the new class.
- **Speed:** look at history only for files that differ, and stop at the first matching version.

## Files to modify

- `scripts/sync-core.sh`: classification, the stop before writing, `--discard-local`, the usage text.
- `.github/workflows/starter-sync.yml`: `fetch-depth: 0` on the starter checkout; the class in the issue body.
- `DEVELOPMENT.md` → Starter sync: the four classes and what to do about each.
- `changelog.txt` (and `README.md`'s changelog if it mirrors Unreleased, as #461 did): one Unreleased line.

Everything stays a core file, so it reaches the plugins through the usual sync.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `scripts/sync-core.sh`
- EDIT: `.github/workflows/starter-sync.yml`
- EDIT: `DEVELOPMENT.md`
- EDIT: `changelog.txt`
- EDIT: `README.md`

## Verification

Use a throwaway plugin made from the starter (`scripts/rename-plugin.sh`) in a temp folder, with a full clone of the starter:

1. **Behind:** the plugin's core files come from an older starter commit; sync from `main`. They are reported as behind and updated, as today.
2. **Newer:** the plugin is synced from `main`; then run `--check --ref v1.0.34`. The updater files are listed as newer and the exit code is 1. Then sync with `--ref v1.0.34`: it writes nothing (`git status` stays clean), exits 2 and says to sync from `main` or a later tag.
3. **Changed here:** change a core file outside its own blocks. `--check` says changed here; a sync writes nothing and exits 2; `--discard-local` replaces the file.
4. **Own blocks only:** a change inside `{css}-own` blocks still matches, as today.
5. **Old workflow copies:** run the old `sed` pattern and `tail -n 1` from today's `starter-sync.yml` on the new `--check` output. They give the same file list and summary as before.
6. **Shallow clone:** `--check` from a `--depth 1` starter clone still lists the files, with class unknown.
7. **Real case:** in a SEO Pro Stats checkout of `main`, `--check --ref v1.0.34` lists `includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php` and `load.php` as newer.

`scripts/lint.sh` passes (ShellCheck).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No sync replaces a core file that is newer than `--ref` or changed only in the plugin, unless `--discard-local` is given (and that option covers changed-here files only).
- [ ] Files that are behind or missing sync as today, and all core files still sync in one run.
- [ ] Today's `--check` lines and last-line summary parse the same way with the old `starter-sync.yml` pattern.
- [ ] The weekly Starter sync issue shows each file's class.
- [ ] `DEVELOPMENT.md` explains the classes; `changelog.txt` has an Unreleased line.

## PR Conventions

One PR that resolves this issue. Plugins pick it up with their next core sync.

title: t10: Network sites: lock remember() and sync() writes of SEEN so Make every site the same keeps before values
body:
## Task


`Network_Sites::remember()` and `Network_Sites::sync()` both rewrite a site's `SEEN` option without a shared lock, so the `before` values that "Make every site the same" records can be lost.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`Network_Sites::remember()` and `Network_Sites::sync()` both rewrite a site's `SEEN` option without a shared lock, so the `before` values that "Make every site the same" records can be lost.

## Why

`sync()` reads `SEEN` (`self::seen()`), then writes it back as `array('version' => ..., 'enforced' => ...)` — without `before`. `remember()` (called by `Network_Differences::copy()`) reads `SEEN` straight from the target site's options table, merges `before`, and writes it back. Neither holds a lock.

In the order `sync()` reads → `remember()` writes → `sync()` writes, the new `before` values are dropped. The site then compares its features' last-saved values against values the network already replaced, finds no change, and skips its saving work for the copy (for example, rewriting a collector config or flushing a page cache) until the next settings change.

The window is narrow (an admin, cron or WP-CLI request on the target site while a network administrator runs Make every site the same), but the outcome is silent stale state.

Found by review on the downstream starter sync (wpallstars/seoprostats PR #292, for wpallstars/seoprostats#290). Per `STANDARDS.md`, core files change in the starter first, then sync downstream.

## How

`includes/class-wpstarter-network-sites.php` holds `sync()` and `remember()`; `includes/class-wpstarter-settings.php` holds `replace_site_values()` and its `lock($table)` (the per-site save lock); `includes/class-wpstarter-network-differences.php` holds `copy()`, the caller of `remember()`.

Preferred approach: do the `SEEN` read-merge-write of `remember()` inside `replace_site_values()` under the same `lock($table)`, and take that lock around `sync()`'s read and its write of `SEEN` (merging rather than discarding a `before` written since its read). Alternative: in `sync()`, re-read `SEEN` under the lock and keep any `before` that was not part of the snapshot it is consuming.

Keep: visitor requests never take the lock (`saving_request()` already excludes them); no new queries on visitor pages.

### Files Scope

- includes/class-wpstarter-network-sites.php
- includes/class-wpstarter-settings.php
- includes/class-wpstarter-network-differences.php

## Acceptance

- With the lock in place, a `remember()` that lands between `sync()`'s read and write is not lost: the next `sync()` on that site runs the saving work for the copied keys.
- `scripts/lint.sh` passes; `scripts/smoke-test.sh` passes, including the multisite path.
- After merge, sync the change into downstream plugins with `scripts/sync-core.sh`.

## Verification

Reproduce on a disposable multisite: hold `sync()` between its read and write (for example, a temporary `sleep()` in a scratch copy), run Make every site the same for a key with a saving hook in another request, release `sync()`, then load the target site's admin and confirm the saving hook ran for that key.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

## Brief Workflow

This issue body is composed under `.agents/workflows/brief.md`. Newly queued auto-dispatch work must pass its `Dispatch Readiness Contract (brief schema v2)`: complete write surface, hazards and compatibility, executable verification mapped to affected surfaces, and positive plus negative/regression acceptance criteria.

</details>

body:
## What

`scripts/smoke-test.sh` gets a `--multisite` mode (and CI runs it once), so the network core files (`WPStarter_Network_Settings`, `WPStarter_Network_Sites`, `WPStarter_Network_Differences`, the network screen) are smoke-tested like the single-site path.

## Why

#469's acceptance asked for "`scripts/smoke-test.sh` passes, including the multisite path", but the script installs a single site only. For #469 (PR #470) the multisite path was verified with a scratch WP-CLI setup instead. Every plugin made from the starter ships these classes, and a fatal error or a full-table query on a network admin screen would pass today's smoke test.

## How

- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` (`start_site()`, `parse_args()`, `usage()`, the page lists): with `--multisite`, run `wp core multisite-install` (subdirectories) instead of `core install`, create a second site (`wp site create --slug=two`), and network-activate the plugin. Then load, as admin: the network settings screen (`/wp-admin/network/settings.php?page=…`, from the plugin's menu slug as `find_plugin_pages()` finds the site screen), each site's settings screen, and the visitor pages on both sites. Keep the existing checks: debug.log empty, no 5xx/critical error page, and the EXPLAIN checks for the plugin's own queries (`scripts/smoke-queries.php`).
- Exercise the network path once with WP-CLI: `WPStarter_Network_Settings::set_value()` and `apply()` for a setting the smoke test registers (or skip with a note when the starter has no settings), then a request on site two so `WPStarter_Network_Sites::sync()` runs, and uninstall cleans `wpstarter_network`, each site's `wpstarter_network_seen` and `wpstarter_network_lock`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` smoke job (`Smoke test (WordPress ${{ matrix.wp }}, PHP ${{ matrix.php }})`): add one matrix entry with `--multisite` (WordPress latest, PHP 8.3), keeping the job's runtime reasonable (`--posts` lower if needed).
- `DEVELOPMENT.md`: mention `--multisite` where the smoke test is described.
- It is a core script (`scripts/core-files.txt`): plugins get it with `scripts/sync-core.sh`. Keep names as placeholders via `scripts/lib/plugin.sh` like the rest of the script.

- `scripts/smoke-test.sh`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- `DEVELOPMENT.md`

title: feat: scripts/deploy-sites.sh rolls a published release out to every install on one SSH host
body:
## What

Add a core script, `scripts/deploy-sites.sh`, that installs a published release zip on every WordPress install on one SSH host that already has the plugin, and a step in `RELEASING.md` that uses it after the update test. Every plugin made from the starter gets it through `scripts/sync-core.sh`.

## Why

Owners roll each release out to their own sites straight after publishing. So far each rollout used a one-off script written on the server (SEO Pro Stack 1.3.31 and 1.3.43, SEO Pro Stats 1.2.0 to 1.4.3). Each did the same steps, re-invented every time: back up the plugin folder, record the `error_log` length, `wp plugin install <zip> --force`, load WordPress once, then check version, status, home page and new log lines. A core script makes it one tested command with the same checks every time.

## How

Files:

- New `scripts/deploy-sites.sh` (core file): add it to `scripts/core-files.txt`.
- `RELEASING.md` → GitHub release: new step 5 after `scripts/update-test.sh`.
- `DEVELOPMENT.md` or `RELEASING.md` → Scripts table: one row for the script.

Behaviour (proven in the SEO Pro Stack 1.3.43 rollout to 15 installs, 3 of them multisite networks; reference implementation below):

- Usage: `scripts/deploy-sites.sh --host <ssh-alias> --tag vX.Y.Z [--parent '~/domains/*/public_html'] [--skip <docroot-name>]... [--dry-run]`.
- Runs locally: downloads `{slug}-X.Y.Z.zip` from the release with `gh release download`, checks its SHA-256 against the asset's GitHub digest and, when a provenance bundle exists, `gh attestation verify`. Copies the zip and the remote part to a private directory on the host (`chmod 700`, files `600`), and checks the SHA-256 again there.
- `--dry-run` (the default without `--apply`) lists each install found (docroot, current version, multisite or not) and stops. Only installs that already have `wp-content/plugins/{slug}/{slug}.php` are touched; the plugin is never added anywhere.
- Per install: tar backup of the plugin folder named `{slug}-<docroot>-<old version>.tar.gz`; `error_log` line count; `wp --skip-plugins --skip-themes plugin install <zip> --force` (activation state is kept, network activation too); one full `wp eval` load so the plugin's settings upgrade runs; then one line: docroot, old → new version, status (`active` / `active-network`), home page HTTP code after redirects, new `error_log` lines.
- Exit non-zero if any install did not reach the version or has new log lines; print the backup directory and the restore command (`tar -xzf` into `wp-content/plugins` after removing the folder).
- Do not use `wp plugin update`: on hosts with HTTP request limiters the update check from WP-CLI reports "already updated" (see aidevops `tools/wordpress/wp-cli-reference.md`). Do not use process substitution (`/dev/fd` is missing in some SSH sessions).
- Keep host names, docroots and backups out of the repository and out of issues: the script takes them as arguments only.

Reference implementation (the server-side part used for 1.3.43; generalise the slug and add the local download/verify part):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Usage: sps-deploy.sh VERSION ZIP BACKUP_DIR
set -uo pipefail

main() {
	local want="$1"
	local zip="$2"
	local backups="$3"
	local d r plugin before v status home code lines_before lines_after

	mkdir -p "$backups" && chmod 700 "$backups"
	cd "$HOME/domains" || return 1
	for r in "$HOME"/domains/*/public_html; do
		d="$(basename "$(dirname "$r")")"
		plugin="$r/wp-content/plugins/seoprostack"
		if [[ ! -f "$r/wp-config.php" || ! -f "$plugin/seoprostack.php" ]]; then
			continue
		fi
		before="$(grep -m1 'Version:' "$plugin/seoprostack.php" | tr -d ' *' | cut -d: -f2)"
		lines_before="$(cat "$r/error_log" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
		tar -czf "$backups/seoprostack-$d-$before.tar.gz" -C "$r/wp-content/plugins" seoprostack && chmod 600 "$backups/seoprostack-$d-$before.tar.gz"
		wp --path="$r" --skip-plugins --skip-themes plugin install "$zip" --force >/dev/null 2>&1
		# A full load runs the plugin's settings upgrade on this (main) site.
		wp --path="$r" eval 'echo "loaded";' >/dev/null 2>&1
		v="$(grep -m1 'Version:' "$plugin/seoprostack.php" | tr -d ' *' | cut -d: -f2)"
		# "active-network" on multisite networks.
		status="$(wp --path="$r" --skip-plugins --skip-themes plugin list --name=seoprostack --field=status 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)"
		home="$(wp --path="$r" --skip-plugins --skip-themes option get home 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)"
		code="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -L -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 30 "$home/")"
		lines_after="$(cat "$r/error_log" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
		printf '%s\t%s -> %s\twant=%s\tstatus=%s\thome=%s\tnew_error_log_lines=%s\n' "$d" "$before" "$v" "$want" "$status" "$code" "$((lines_after - lines_before))"
	done
	return 0
}

main "$@"
```

Related: aidevops `wp-fleet-helper.sh` (plan / backup / deploy / verify / report with a reviewed plan fingerprint, `--discover-ssh` for hosts without a site list) covers the same need for operators with aidevops. Mention it in the new `RELEASING.md` step as the alternative; this script is the starter's self-contained path.

## Acceptance

- `scripts/deploy-sites.sh` in the starter and in `scripts/core-files.txt`; ShellCheck clean; every function ends with an explicit `return`.
- Dry run lists installs and changes nothing; `--apply` backs up, installs and reports one line per install, and exits non-zero on any version mismatch or new log lines.
- `RELEASING.md` step 5 and the Scripts table describe it; `scripts/preflight-release.sh` still passes.
- After merge, offspring plugins (SEO Pro Stack, SEO Pro Stats) pick it up through their usual `starter-sync` issue.

### Files Scope

- NEW: `scripts/deploy-sites.sh`
- EDIT: `scripts/core-files.txt`
- EDIT: `RELEASING.md`
- EDIT: `DEVELOPMENT.md`

## Verification

- `shellcheck scripts/deploy-sites.sh`.
- Disposable test: `scripts/update-test.sh`'s Docker WordPress, or any test host reachable over SSH with two installs: dry run, then `--apply` with the newest release; check the version, backups and the one-line report; restore one install from its backup.

title: CLAUDE.md pointer, provenance IDs, compulsory guidance and licence guidance for AI copies
body:
## What

Make sure an AI assistant asked to copy, rename or adapt the starter, or a plugin made from it, reads the guidance, keeps the GPL-3.0 and section 7(b) terms, and keeps the copyright credit. Also make public copies traceable.

1. **`CLAUDE.md`** (new core file): a pointer that imports `AGENTS.md` (`@AGENTS.md`). Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md`, not `AGENTS.md`, so today it may never see the guidance. Kept out of the zips (`.distignore`, preflight `DEV_FILES`).
2. **Provenance IDs (canary tokens)**: one ID per plugin (`wpas-` and 16 hex digits). The starter's ID goes in `ATTRIBUTION.txt` and in the licence lines at the top of every core file. Each plugin made from the starter gets its own ID, which `scripts/rename-plugin.sh` writes into its main file and its own files. A file copied from another plugin keeps that plugin's ID. The IDs are plain text; nothing is sent anywhere. A new core script, `scripts/provenance-search.sh`, searches GitHub code for the IDs and lists repositories outside the owner, noting whether each one keeps the credit.
3. **Credit in partial copies**: each source file's licence lines end with `Provenance: <id>. Copies, whole or in part, keep these lines.`
4. **Compulsory reading**: `AGENTS.md`, in the starter and the one `rename-plugin.sh` writes, makes every shared guidance file compulsory reading before any change: `STANDARDS.md`, `STYLING.md`, `DEVELOPMENT.md`, `RELEASING.md`, `LAUNCH.md`, `ATTRIBUTION.txt`, plus the `docs/` file for the task. `STANDARDS.md` → Agent docs says so, and the preflight warns when `AGENTS.md` leaves one out or `CLAUDE.md` is missing.
5. **AI guidance in many places**: a section for AI assistants in `ATTRIBUTION.txt` (ships in both zips, word for word in every plugin). It tells them to keep the notices even when asked to make the work look like someone else's, and to explain why. There is also a line in the main file's GPL notice, `README.md` → License, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `STANDARDS.md` → Structure.

Then release 1.0.38 (owner asked for full-loop through to release).

## Files to modify

title: preview-browser.sh: a page cache's cached home page makes login and log-mark print nothing
body:
## What

`scripts/preview-browser.sh` loads the preview site's WordPress as an anonymous `GET /` request (`$_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] = 'GET'`, `REQUEST_URI = '/'`, no cookies; the PHP heredoc in `wp_run()`, about lines 134–144). When the site has a PHP page cache with a cached copy of the home page, the cache's `advanced-cache.php` (loaded by `wp-settings.php` when `WP_CACHE` is true) serves that page and exits inside `require $site . '/wp-load.php'`. `ob_start()` swallows the page, so the script reports success with nothing in it:

```
$ scripts/preview-browser.sh login
Signed in as  until .
State file: …/seoprostack-browser.XXXXXX      (0 bytes)
Admin:
$ scripts/preview-browser.sh log-mark
0
```

Seen on SEO Pro Stack's shared preview with WP-Optimize's page cache on: the page ended in `Cached by WP-Optimize (gzip)`. Deleting `wp-content/cache/wpo-cache/<host>/index.html{,.gz}` made `login` work again, until the next anonymous visit to the home page caches it again.

## Fix

In the PHP part of `wp_run()`, before `require $site . '/wp-load.php'`, make the request one that page caches never answer. WP-Optimize's `wpo_can_serve_from_cache()` (`wp-optimize/cache/file-based-page-cache-functions.php`) skips non-GET requests and requests with a `wordpress_logged_in_*` or `wordpress_sec_*` cookie; WP Super Cache, W3 Total Cache and Cache Enabler skip logged-in cookies too. Recommended: set a cookie whose name starts with `wordpress_logged_in_` but is not WordPress's real `LOGGED_IN_COOKIE` (for example `$_COOKIE['wordpress_logged_in_preview_browser'] = '1';`). WordPress validates only its own hashed cookie name, so nobody is signed in by it. Comment why. Then:

1. Make the script fail loudly instead of printing empty values: after `wp-load.php`, if `did_action( 'wp_loaded' )` is 0, or `login` gets no user, call `preview_fail()`, and have the shell side treat empty output from `login` as an error (no 0-byte state file left behind).
2. Sync to the plugins (`scripts/sync-core.sh`), as usual for a core file.

Files: `scripts/preview-browser.sh` only; `DEVELOPMENT.md` → Checking screens in a browser may say that page caches are bypassed.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh shell` passes (ShellCheck).
- On a test site with WP-Optimize's page cache on, open the home page once signed out (so `wp-content/cache/wpo-cache/<host>/index.html` exists), then `scripts/preview-browser.sh login` prints the user, expiry and admin URL, the state file is non-empty, `log-mark` prints the log's real line count, and `logout` works.
- With the cached page present and the fix's cookie line removed, `login` exits non-zero with a `preview-browser:` message instead of empty output.

title: feat: preflight warns when plugin code reuses core header class names
body:
## What

Add a release preflight check that warns when a plugin's own code uses a class name that a starter core stylesheet already styles, so plugin screens never inherit core header styles by accident.

## Why (observed)

In SEO Pro Stats, the Search screen's report-tab row used `.spst-subnav`. After a starter core sync, the core `admin/css/{slug}-header.css` styled `.{css}-subnav` as the screen header's second row (`padding: 8px 24px; background: var(--{css}-subtle)`). Inside the plugin's React app `--{css}-subtle` is a text grey, so the row became a grey bar with faint tabs, most visible in dark mode. Nothing flagged it: lint, build, preflight, Plugin Check and CI all passed. Fixed in the plugin by renaming its class (`.spst-search-nav`), released as SEO Pro Stats 1.8.3 (wpallstars/seoprostats#320, PR wpallstars/seoprostats#321).

The core header classes are short, generic names likely to be reused: in this repo, `admin/css/wpstarter-header.css` styles `.wps-wrap`, `.wps-header`, `.wps-nav`, `.wps-subnav`, `.wps-main`, plus their `__` elements.

## How

- `scripts/preflight-release.sh`: add `check_core_class_names` next to `check_core_files` (around line 788), reusing `section` / `ok` / `warn`.
  - Collect the block-level class names from core stylesheets listed in `scripts/core-files.txt` (at least `admin/css/{slug}-header.css`): selectors `\.{css}-[a-z0-9-]+` that have no `__` element suffix.
  - Search the plugin's own (non-core) source at the release ref (`git grep` on `$sha`, for example `*.php`, `*.js`, `*.ts`, `*.tsx`, `*.css`, excluding `assets/build/`, `vendor/`, `node_modules/` and core files) for those names used as class names (`className="…"`, `class="…"`, CSS selectors).
  - Uses that the core files expect (for example the `render_header()` markup in a core file) are not plugin-own and are skipped because core files are excluded.
  - Warn (not error) with `file:line` and the class name, suggesting a screen-specific name such as `.{css}-<screen>-nav`.
- `STANDARDS.md` → front-end styling: one line saying plugin-own code must not reuse core header class names (`{css}-wrap`, `-header`, `-nav`, `-subnav`, `-main`), and that preflight warns.
- Bring the check to the plugins made from the starter with `scripts/sync-core.sh`, as with other core changes.

Paths are known; the exact core class list should be derived at run time from the stylesheet, not hard-coded.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `scripts/preflight-release.sh`
- EDIT: `STANDARDS.md`
- EDIT: `changelog.txt`

## Verification

- `shellcheck scripts/preflight-release.sh` clean; `scripts/lint.sh` passes.
- In a throwaway branch, add `<div class="wps-subnav">` to a non-core admin file: `scripts/preflight-release.sh` prints a `warn` naming that file and line. Remove it: the section prints `ok`.

title: fix: deploy-sites.sh checks each site's real PHP log destinations (custom WP_DEBUG_LOG, error_log)
body:
## What

Make `scripts/deploy-sites.sh --apply` check each site's real PHP log destinations. Today it counts new lines only in the docroot's `error_log` and in `wp-content/debug.log`. When `WP_DEBUG_LOG` is a custom path, as Debug Log Manager sets in `wp-config.php`, or PHP's `error_log` setting names another file, a warning or fatal error the update causes is never seen, and the install is reported `ok`.

## Why

During the SEO Pro Stack 1.3.47 rollout, one of 15 installs had a custom `WP_DEBUG_LOG` path, and the preview site uses one too. Their `new_log_lines=0` covered only the two fixed files, so a separate manual pass over the real destinations was needed to confirm the deploy. The deploy is meant to fail on new log lines, so this is a gap in its own check.

## How

Files to modify:

- `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`, the core file shared by every plugin: `new_log_text()` (around line 91), `file_lines()` callers in the per-install block (around lines 160–187).
- `RELEASING.md`, in the Scripts table row for `scripts/deploy-sites.sh`: say it watches the site's PHP logs (`WP_DEBUG_LOG`, including a custom path, and PHP's `error_log`).

Approach:

1. Before the install, find the destinations once with the existing `wp_bare` helper (`--skip-plugins --skip-themes`), for example `wp_bare "$root" eval 'echo (defined("WP_DEBUG_LOG") && is_string(WP_DEBUG_LOG) && !in_array(strtolower(WP_DEBUG_LOG), array("1","true"), true)) ? WP_DEBUG_LOG : (defined("WP_DEBUG_LOG") && WP_DEBUG_LOG ? WP_CONTENT_DIR . "/debug.log" : "");'` and `wp_bare "$root" eval 'echo ini_get("error_log");'`.
2. Keep the docroot `error_log` and `wp-content/debug.log`, add the found paths, and drop duplicates and non-files. A relative `error_log` value is relative to the PHP process; resolve it against the docroot or skip it.
3. Count lines before and after for each file, as `file_lines` does now, and print the first new lines from every file in `new_log_text`.
4. Never print a path in the summary line; host folders stay out of output that may be pasted into issues (`RELEASING.md` → step 5).

Hazards: some shared hosts' jailed shells have no `/dev/fd`, so don't use `< <(...)` in the remote script; use pipes or variables. PHP `shell_exec` and `proc_open` may be disabled, so stay with plain `wp eval`. Keep Bash 3.2 compatibility and explicit `return 0` in every function, as the file does now.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`
- EDIT: `RELEASING.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- A site whose `WP_DEBUG_LOG` is a custom path, gaining a PHP warning during the deploy, gets `FAIL` with the new lines printed.
- Sites with the default destinations behave as before.
- No folder paths appear in the summary lines.
- `shellcheck scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh scripts/deploy-sites.sh` and `scripts/lint.sh` pass.

## Verification

- On a disposable WordPress (as `scripts/update-test.sh` builds), set `define('WP_DEBUG_LOG', WP_CONTENT_DIR . '/uploads/custom-debug.log');`, add a mu-plugin that calls `trigger_error('canary', E_USER_WARNING)`, and run the remote part against it. The install must report `FAIL` and show the canary line.
- Then sync the change to plugins made from the starter (`DEVELOPMENT.md` → Starter sync).

title: Add scripts/test-site.sh: a disposable WordPress kept running for one branch's build
body:
## What

Add a core script, `scripts/test-site.sh`, that starts a disposable WordPress in Docker with the plugin built from one Git ref, **keeps it running** for manual and agent checks (WP-CLI, REST, wp-admin in a browser), and removes it on request.

## Why

Plugins made from this starter have three Docker scripts, and every one removes its site when it finishes: `scripts/smoke-test.sh`, `scripts/update-test.sh` and `scripts/plugin-check.sh`. `scripts/preview-site.sh` copies a combined preview (origin/main plus every open PR) onto the one shared local test site, so it cannot test one branch alone and must not be reset.

While building a feature in a plugin made from this starter (a crawl-export import with REST, WP-CLI, abilities, undo and demo data), the agent had to write a throwaway script to get a site it could keep running for a single commit: import files, call REST with multipart uploads, run WP-CLI, rebuild and reinstall after each fix, then remove everything. That script worked; it should be a reusable core script, not reinvented each time.

## How

New file `scripts/test-site.sh` (a core file: add it to `scripts/core-files.txt`, so `scripts/sync-core.sh` copies it to every plugin). Subcommands:

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `up [--ref REF] [--wp VERSION] [--php VERSION] [--multisite]` | Creates a Docker network, volume, MariaDB and `wordpress:php<V>-apache` container, all labelled; installs WordPress with `WP_DEBUG`, `WP_DEBUG_LOG`, `WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY=false`, `SAVEQUERIES` and pretty permalinks; builds the zip with `scripts/build-release.sh --ref REF --quiet` and installs and activates it. Prints the site address (port bound to 127.0.0.1 only) and the admin login. |
| `reinstall [--ref REF]` | Rebuilds the zip from REF (default `HEAD`) and runs `wp plugin install --force --activate`. |
| `wp ARGS...` | Runs WP-CLI in the site (a `wordpress:cli` container on the same network and volume, user 33). A read-only folder (such as `--files DIR`, mounted at `/files`) makes local import files reachable. |
| `url` | Prints the address. |
| `log` | Prints `wp-content/debug.log`. |
| `down` | Removes every container, volume and network with the site's label, then says so. |

Rules:

title: CI: survive Docker Hub 429 rate limits (actionlint, smoke test, Plugin Check)
body:
## What

Make CI stop failing when Docker Hub refuses anonymous pulls from GitHub's runners (HTTP 429 Too Many Requests). Every Docker-based CI step pulls from Docker Hub without logging in: actionlint (`rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`), and the WordPress, WP-CLI and MariaDB images in `scripts/smoke-test.sh` and `scripts/plugin-check.sh` (`wordpress:cli-php…`, `wordpress:php…-apache`, `mariadb:10.6`; the latter two already read `<PREFIX>_CLI_IMAGE` / `<PREFIX>_DB_IMAGE`).

## Why (observed)

On 16 Oct 2026 from about 00:30 UTC, every CI run in a plugin made from this starter failed before testing anything: `main` (run 38829936347: Plugin Check and both smoke tests, `docker.io/library/mariadb:10.6` → 429) and a pull request (run 38830560657, twice: actionlint `docker.io/rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12` → 429, which as the first lint step also skips the smoke and release jobs). The code itself passed the same checks locally. A shared runner IP's anonymous pull budget is outside our control, so this will recur in every copy of the starter.

## How

These files are core files (`scripts/core-files.txt`), so change them here and let each plugin's starter sync pick them up.

1. **actionlint without Docker:** install the pinned release binary (version 1.7.12, verified against the release's published checksum) in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, or use a pinned action that does so; run it the same way (`-color`, whole repository).
2. **Images through a mirror, or logged in:** before the Docker steps in the smoke, Plugin Check and release jobs, either configure the runner's Docker daemon with a Docker Hub pull-through mirror (for example Google's public mirror of Docker Hub; verify its current address in Google's documentation) or log in to Docker Hub when repository secrets for it exist (skip the login when they do not, so forks still run). Prefer the option that needs no secret.
3. **One retry with backoff** for pulls in `scripts/smoke-test.sh` and `scripts/plugin-check.sh` (for example `docker pull` up to 3 times, 20 s apart, before `docker run`), so a brief 429 does not fail the job. Keep local runs unchanged apart from the retry.
4. Note the change and the `*_IMAGE` overrides in `DEVELOPMENT.md` where CI is described.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- EDIT: `scripts/smoke-test.sh`
- EDIT: `scripts/plugin-check.sh`
- EDIT: `DEVELOPMENT.md`

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh workflows` and ShellCheck (`scripts/lint.sh shell`) pass.
- CI on the PR runs actionlint, the smoke tests (WordPress 6.2/PHP 7.4, latest/PHP 8.3, multisite) and Plugin Check to completion.
- After a starter sync, a plugin made from the starter (for example SEO Pro Stats) shows the same in its CI.

`scripts/replaced-plugins.php --write` writes ungrammatical README lines when only one plugin is replaced, or only one replaced plugin can be downloaded.

title: fix: GitHub updater reads a deleted plugin's headers after wp plugin uninstall
body:
## What

`wp plugin uninstall <plugin>` logs a PHP warning from the shared GitHub updater when another plugin made from the starter is active:

```text
PHP Warning:  file_get_contents(/var/www/html/wp-content/plugins/<deleted>/<deleted>.php): Failed to open stream: No such file or directory in wp-includes/functions.php on line 7038
```

Seen on WordPress 7.1.3, PHP 8.2 and WP-CLI's `wordpress:cli-php8.2` image while checking a plugin rename in SEO Pro Stats (GH#376 there): the old copy was uninstalled with WP-CLI while the renamed plugin was active. The data was not affected; the warning lands in `debug.log` and fails any check that expects an empty log.

## Why it happens (backtrace from a must-use error handler)

```text
get_file_data                                   class-wpallstars-github-updater.php:373
WPAllStars_GitHub_Updater::from_headers         class-wpallstars-github-updater.php:339
WPAllStars_GitHub_Updater::plugins              class-wpallstars-github-updater.php:876
WPAllStars_GitHub_Updater::add_updates          (pre_set_site_transient_update_plugins)
set_site_transient                              WP-CLI Plugin_Command.php:1261
Plugin_Command->uninstall
```

WP-CLI deletes the plugin's files, then saves the `update_plugins` site transient. `plugins()` builds its list from `get_plugins()`, whose per-request cache (`wp_cache` group `plugins`) still names the deleted plugin, and `from_headers()` reads that file's headers without checking it exists. It shows only when `update_plugins` is already set (after any admin request), which is why a fresh site does not show it.

## How to fix

`includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php`, `from_headers()` (near line 369): return `null` before `get_file_data()` when `! is_file( WP_PLUGIN_DIR . '/' . $file )`, with a comment saying why (a plugin deleted earlier in the request is still in `get_plugins()`' cache). Keep `plugins()` as it is. Then sync to the plugins made from the starter with `scripts/sync-core.sh`.

### Files Scope

- `includes/github-updater/class-wpallstars-github-updater.php`
- `includes/github-updater/load.php`

Integration scope recovery: `STANDARDS.md` (Updates from GitHub) and `load.php` require raising the shared updater version with every change. The loader chooses the highest registered version across active plugins; without a bump, an unchanged copy can win and retain the warning. Raise 1.6.2 to 1.6.3. No open PR or pushed issue branch overlaps these paths at pickup. Verify both files with `scripts/lint.sh` and exercise uninstall with another starter-made plugin active on a disposable site. Downstream syncs remain separate repository work; this issue delivers the master core fix.

## Verify

1. A disposable site with two starter-made plugins; activate one; open any admin page (sets `update_plugins`).
2. `wp plugin uninstall <the other one>` with `WP_DEBUG_LOG` on: `debug.log` stays empty after the fix (shows the warning before).
3. `scripts/lint.sh` (phpcs, phpstan) passes.

title: update-test.sh: ignore WP-CLI's own phar deprecations in the debug.log check
body:
## Problem

`scripts/update-test.sh` reports a false failure: "PHP messages in debug.log". On 2026-10-17, a plugin made from this starter (0.1.0 → 0.1.1, WordPress 7.1.3, PHP 8.3) passed every update check (offer, Updates screen, Plugins screen, install, still active, settings screen). It still failed, because `debug.log` held 14 `PHP Deprecated` lines, all from WP-CLI's own phar:

```
PHP Deprecated:  Return type of Symfony\Component\Finder\Finder::getIterator() should either be compatible with IteratorAggregate::getIterator(): Traversable ... in phar:///usr/local/bin/wp/vendor/symfony/finder/Finder.php on line 566
```

`wp_cli()` (`scripts/update-test.sh:128-133`) runs the `wordpress:cli-php$PHP_VERSION` image against the same `wp-content`. The site has `WP_DEBUG_LOG` on, so the CLI process's deprecations from `wp plugin update` (line 338, which loads Symfony Finder) go into the site's `debug.log`. `check_debug_log()` (lines 367-387) then counts them as the plugin's.

## Fix

In `check_debug_log()`, next to the canary filter at line 380, also drop lines whose file is WP-CLI's phar. Use `grep -v -F 'phar:///usr/local/bin/wp/'`, after the canary check, so a missing canary is still caught. Messages from the plugin, WordPress or other plugins are still reported. Do not lower `error_reporting` for `wp_cli`: that would also hide the plugin's own deprecations during the update.

Check `scripts/smoke-test.sh` for the same pattern. It passed in the same session, but it may not run `wp plugin update`.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `scripts/update-test.sh`
- EDIT: `scripts/smoke-test.sh` (only if it has the same check)

## Verification

- `shellcheck scripts/update-test.sh`
- In a plugin made from the starter with at least two releases: `WPALLSTARS_GITHUB_TOKEN=… scripts/update-test.sh --from <previous> --to <latest>` ends with "no PHP messages (the canary notice arrived)".

title: deploy-sites.sh: purge page caches after install so new asset versions reach visitors
body:
## What happens

`scripts/deploy-sites.sh --apply` replaces the plugin files but leaves page caches alone. WordPress versions plugin assets by file time or version (`?ver=...`), so the old page HTML that LiteSpeed Cache keeps serving still points at the previous asset URL. The browser and CDN copy for that URL is the old file, so visitors keep the old CSS/JS until the page cache expires. The deploy reports `home=200 ... ok` regardless.

Seen with SEO Pro Cookie Consent 0.1.4 (a CSS-only fix). After a successful deploy to 14 installs, a listing page returned `x-litespeed-cache: hit` with `spcc.css?ver=<old mtime>` and the old rule. It was fixed only after `wp litespeed-purge all` on every site, including every site of each multisite network (network-activated LiteSpeed too).

## Fix (starter core file; sync to plugins afterwards)

In `scripts/deploy-sites.sh`, after a successful install, for each site of the install (`wp site list --field=url` on a network, else home):

- if `wp --url=<site> cli has-command litespeed-purge` succeeds, run `wp --url=<site> litespeed-purge all`
- add `purged=<n>/<sites>` to the per-install line

Optionally do the same for other page caches with WP-CLI purge commands (`wp cache flush` is object cache only, so it isn't enough). Use `cli has-command`, not `plugin is-active`: per-site `is-active` missed a network-activated LiteSpeed in practice.

Document it in `RELEASING.md` → GitHub release step 5.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `scripts/deploy-sites.sh`
- EDIT: `RELEASING.md`

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh shell`
- Deploy to a host with LiteSpeed: the per-install line shows the purge count. A cached page fetched afterwards shows `x-litespeed-cache: miss` and the new `?ver=`.

title: fix: release tag on a [skip ci] metrics commit never starts the Release workflow
body:
## What

A release tag on a `[skip ci]` commit never starts the Release workflow. Make the release steps tag a commit that runs it, have the preflight warn before tagging, and give `release.yml` a manual way to run on an existing tag.

## Why

Observed during a 1.0.0 release of a plugin built from this starter: the release PR merged, the Repository metrics workflow then pushed its badge refresh to `main` as `chore(metrics): refresh repository metrics [skip ci]`, and RELEASING.md step 3 (`git tag -a vX.Y.Z origin/main`) tagged that commit. The tag pushed fine, but no Release run appeared. GitHub applies `[skip ci]` (and `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]`) in the head commit message to push events, tag pushes included. `scripts/preflight-release.sh --ref origin/main` passed (0 errors), so nothing warned before the tag. The release had to be published by hand with the step 3 fallback (`scripts/build-release.sh --ref vX.Y.Z` + `gh release create`). In a public plugin that also loses the Sigstore provenance, and with no failed run there is nothing to **Re-run** to get it.

The metrics workflow runs after every push to `main`, so the newest commit on `main` is often a `[skip ci]` one just after a merge. Every plugin using the starter can hit this.

## How (Approach)

Recommended, all three in one PR:

1. **`scripts/preflight-release.sh` → `check_git()` (around line 1245)**: read the commit message of `$sha` (`git log -1 --format=%B "$sha"`). If it contains any of the GitHub skip markers above (case-insensitive), `warn` (an error when the `v$version` tag already points at it): "{ref} is a [skip ci] commit: a tag on it does not start the Release workflow; tag the release PR's merge commit instead". Follow the existing `ok`/`warn`/`note` style in that function.
2. **`RELEASING.md` step 3 (line 86)**: tag the release PR's merge commit, not whatever `origin/main` is at that moment, e.g. `git tag -a vX.Y.Z "$(gh pr view N --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)" -m "{Name} X.Y.Z"`, and say why in one sentence (metrics commits use `[skip ci]`; they touch only `docs/metrics/`, which is not in the zips). Run the preflight on the same ref. Keep the fallback paragraph and mention option 3.
3. **`.github/workflows/release.yml`**: add `workflow_dispatch` with a required `tag` input. Use `TAG: ${{ inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}` and check out that tag (`ref: refs/tags/${{ inputs.tag }}` when dispatched). Keep the existing "Check the tag" step unchanged so a dispatched run still requires `vX.Y.Z` on `main`. Validate the input through the env var only, never by interpolating it into `run:`. The existing `gh release view` → `upload --clobber` branch already handles a release made by hand first.

### Files to Modify

- `scripts/preflight-release.sh` (`check_git`)
- `RELEASING.md` (GitHub release, step 3)
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` (trigger, `TAG`, checkout ref)

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `scripts/preflight-release.sh`
- EDIT: `RELEASING.md`
- EDIT: `.github/workflows/release.yml`

### Complete Write Surface

The three files above. These are core files, so plugins get them on their next `scripts/sync-core.sh`. No changes to `repo-metrics.yml`: `[skip ci]` there is intended, to avoid CI loops.

### Verification Before Dispatch

- `scripts/lint.sh` (includes actionlint/shellcheck for workflows and scripts).
- Preflight: in a scratch clone, create a commit with `[skip ci]` in its message and run `scripts/preflight-release.sh --ref HEAD --offline --no-docker`; expect the new warning. On a normal commit, no warning.
- Workflow: `actionlint .github/workflows/release.yml`; confirm with the workflow's YAML that a push-tag run still sets `TAG` from `github.ref_name` and a dispatch sets it from the input. Do not push a real release tag for this test.

## Acceptance

- Preflight warns on a `[skip ci]` ref and stays quiet otherwise.
- RELEASING.md step 3 tags the merge commit and explains why in one sentence.
- `release.yml` can be run manually for an existing `vX.Y.Z` tag on `main`, with the same tag checks as a push.
- `scripts/lint.sh` passes.

## Tier

`tier:standard`: three files, known patterns, the approach is decided; workflow trigger and input handling need care.
