title: deploy-sites.sh: check every site of a multisite network, past page caches
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## What

`scripts/deploy-sites.sh --apply` checks each install through its main site only. After this change, the remote part (`scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`) checks every site of a multisite network after the install:

- one full WordPress load per site, under the existing activation guard, so each site's settings upgrade runs;
- the plugin's status on that site;
- that site's home page.

Every home page fetch carries a query string unique to that fetch, so a page cache cannot answer instead of PHP, and the output shows the response's cache headers. A network prints one indented line per site. A site that fails makes its install fail and print the install's restore command. A single-site install still prints one line.

## Why

This showed up when a plugin made from the starter was rolled out to one shared host: 16 installs, 5 of them multisite networks, 31 sites in all (one network has 12 sites). The deploy loaded and fetched only each install's main site, so it checked 16 of the 31 sites. The other 15 network sites had to be checked afterwards with hand-written scripts.

The home check also proves little there. Fetched on that server the way `apply_one()` fetches it (a plain `curl` of the home page, `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh:405-408`), 3 main home pages came back `x-litespeed-cache: hit` twice in a row, and a network site came back `miss`, then `hit`. With a unique query string, all 4 came back `miss`. A cache hit means PHP never ran, so `home=200` says nothing about the new code. Today a fatal error is reported `ok` if it is on a network site other than the main one, or if the page cache hides it.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The behaviour, output fields, failure policy and helper boundaries are decided below. The worker still writes the shell code and runs a disposable Docker check whose URL step the brief author did not run, so the contract is not exact enough for `tier:simple`.

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `deploy-sites multisite per-site home check page cache` → 0 hits; `files_scope_excluded brief repair starter deploy` → 0 hits. No relevant lessons.
- [x] Discovery pass: in the last 48h only PR #516 (e562c05, the activation-list guard) changed `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`, and #516, #518 and #519 changed `RELEASING.md`. All are merged, and every line reference below is from `main` after them. No PR is open. Open #515 (page-cache purge after install) is blocked on its own brief repair and will change the same function (see Dependencies).
- [x] File refs verified: every path and line range below was checked against `main` at 3ae194e on 2026-10-18.
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard`. The disqualifier check is clean: no trust boundary, destructive authority or migration is involved.
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped. The runtime check needs a disposable Docker network that the brief author did not run.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-18
- **Session:** OpenCode, interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive, for the maintainer
- **Blocked by:** none
- **Conversation context:** After a release went out to several multisite networks, every network site had to be checked by hand. The maintainer asked for those checks to run inside the deploy, and for this public issue to contain no private data.

## How (Approach)

### Worker Quick-Start

```bash
# The function to change, and the guard each per-site load must go through:
sed -n '361,432p' scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh   # apply_one()
sed -n '242,254p' scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh   # active_guard ROOT ADD REMOVE WP-ARGS...
sed -n '88,116p'  scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh   # wp_bare (last line only), wp_checked (all lines)
# Gotchas:
# - wp_bare prints only the LAST line of output, so use wp_checked for the site list.
# - active_guard passes its trailing arguments to WP-CLI, so --url=URL works there unchanged.
# - A helper that sets globals (counters, results) must run in the current shell: never
#   inside $(...) or in a "| while" loop. Read lists with done <<<"$list", as main() does.
# - The remote part may not use process substitution (/dev/fd is missing in some SSH
#   sessions); use mktemp files, as wp_checked does.
# - wordpress:cli-php8.3 has bash, curl, tar, sha256sum and wp (checked 2026-10-18).
```

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh:361-432`: in `apply_one()`, replace the main-site load (391-396) and the main-site status read and home fetch (399-408) with the per-site pass, and add the new helpers above `apply_one()`.
- `EDIT: scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh:9-13`: the header says each printed line is one install; add the per-site lines.
- `EDIT: scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh:32`: two new globals next to `FAILED=0`.
- `EDIT: scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh:446-517`: in `main()`, set the run stamp before the install loop.
- `EDIT: scripts/deploy-sites.sh:27-34`: the header comment on what `--apply` checks and prints. `usage()` prints lines 2-39 (`scripts/deploy-sites.sh:77`); if the header changes length, update that range so `--help` still ends with "(RELEASING.md step 5)."
- `EDIT: RELEASING.md:22`: the `deploy-sites.sh` row of the Scripts table.
- `EDIT: RELEASING.md:134-137`: step 5, "Each line gives ...".
- `EDIT: README.md:152`: one `Developers:` bullet at the top of `### Unreleased`.
- `EDIT: changelog.txt:5`: the same entry at the top of `= Unreleased =`.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `scripts/deploy-sites.sh:188-195` (`dry_run()` streams the remote part with `list`) and `scripts/deploy-sites.sh:197-220` (`apply()` copies it to the host and runs `apply`). People read the printed lines (RELEASING.md step 5). A plugin's own fleet script may source the file with `DEPLOY_LIBRARY_ONLY=1` and call `active_guard` (`RELEASING.md:34-37`); in this repository only `RELEASING.md` and `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh` mention `DEPLOY_LIBRARY_ONLY`. Plugins made from the starter get the change through `scripts/sync-core.sh` (`scripts/core-files.txt:41-42`).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** The per-site loads run each site's own plugin code, including its settings upgrade, the same way the main-site load at `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh:391-396` does today. Each load is wrapped in `active_guard` (`:242-254`), and `active_restore_code()` (`:166-193`) stays the only activation-list writer. The home fetches are HTTP GETs. Nothing else writes.
- **Existing verification/tests:** No test or workflow runs the remote part: only `RELEASING.md`, `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `scripts/core-files.txt`, `scripts/deploy-sites.sh` and the file itself mention `deploy-remote`. CI runs ShellCheck on every shell script (`scripts/lint.sh php js shell phpcs phpstan`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:99`). PR #476 checked the original feature with an ad hoc Docker run of single-site and network rollouts.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A because the remote part reads no config file or schema. Its inputs are the positional arguments from `apply()` (`scripts/deploy-sites.sh:211-212`) and the `DEPLOY_WP_CLI` and `DEPLOY_WEB_ERROR_LOG` variables (`scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh:29-30`), which this task leaves alone. No script parses the printed lines: `new_log_lines` appears only in `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `apply()` copies `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh` from the same checkout to the host on every run (`scripts/deploy-sites.sh:208`), so the host never runs an older copy. Plugin copies are updated later by `scripts/sync-core.sh`, outside this task.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because the script stores no data of its own. Each site's settings upgrade is the plugin's own code, which the main-site load already runs today (`scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh:391-396`); see Hazards.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** Unchanged: the per-install tar backup (`scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh:372-378`) and the restore line (`:428-430`). A failing site fails its install, which prints that restore line. Each fetch removes its temporary header file.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add three helpers above `apply_one()`. Skeleton (follow the file's style: `local var="$1"`, explicit `return 0`/`return 1`, tabs):

```bash
# The sites to check, main site first: its home (read as apply_one() reads
# it today), then, on a network, every other site that is not archived,
# deleted or spam. One URL per line. Prints only, so $(...) is fine here.
site_urls() {
	local root="$1"
	local kind="$2"
	local main urls url
	main="$(wp_bare "$root" option get home)" || return 1
	[[ -n "$main" ]] || return 1
	printf '%s\n' "$main"
	[[ "$kind" == "multisite" ]] || return 0
	urls="$(wp_checked "$root" --skip-plugins --skip-themes site list --field=url --archived=0 --deleted=0 --spam=0)" || return 1
	while IFS= read -r url; do
		[[ -n "$url" && "${url%/}" != "${main%/}" ]] || continue
		printf '%s\n' "$url"
	done <<<"$urls"
	return 0
}

# GET one home page past page caches, with a query string unique to this
# fetch. Sets HOME_CODE and HOME_CACHE, so call it directly, never in $(...).
# HOME_CACHE lists the final response's x-litespeed-cache, x-cache and
# cf-cache-status headers, lower-cased, as name:value joined with commas, or
# "none". curl -L writes one header block per hop: keep only the block after
# the last HTTP/ status line.
home_check() {
	local url="$1"
	local headers
	FETCHES=$((FETCHES + 1))
	HOME_CODE="000"
	HOME_CACHE="none"
	headers="$(mktemp)" || return 1
	HOME_CODE="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -L -D "$headers" -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 30 \
		"${url%/}/?deploy-check=${RUN_STAMP}-${FETCHES}" || true)"
	HOME_CACHE="..." # awk over "$headers": reset at each /^HTTP\//, keep the 3 headers
	rm -f "$headers"
	return 0
}

# Read the kind (is_multisite, as list_one() does at :356), then check each
# URL from site_urls "$root" "$kind":
#   load:   active_guard "$root" "" "" [--url="$url"] eval 'echo "loaded";' >/dev/null
#   status: wp_bare "$root" [--url="$url"] plugin list --name="$SLUG" --field=status
#   home:   home_check "$url"
# Pass --url only on a network, so a single site loads exactly as today.
# A site FAILs on a failed load or status read, or on home 5xx or 000; a 4xx
# is only reported (see :416-418). A "hit" in HOME_CACHE is reported as
# "WARN cached" and does not fail. Check every site even after one fails.
# Sets SITES_TOTAL, SITES_FAILED, MAIN_STATUS, MAIN_CODE and MAIN_CACHE (from
# the first row, the main site) and SITE_LINES (networks only, one line per
# site, 4-space indent):
#     site URL<TAB>status=S<TAB>home=CODE<TAB>cache=C<TAB>ok|WARN cached|FAIL: reason
# Returns 1 only when the kind or the site list cannot be read. Call it
# directly, never in $(...).
check_sites() { ... }
```

2. Add the globals `RUN_STAMP=""` and `FETCHES=0` next to `FAILED=0` (`:32`). In `main()`, set `RUN_STAMP="$(date -u +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)-$$"` before the install loop (`:500`).
3. In `apply_one()`: keep the backup, the log baseline and the guarded install (`:371-390`). Replace `:391-396` and `:399-408` with a direct `check_sites "$root"` call. When it returns 1, print `FAIL: cannot list the sites` with the restore line and return 0, as the other failure branches do. Keep the version read (`:398`). Keep computing `new_lines` after the checks (`:409-414`), so log lines that the per-site loads and fetches cause count too. In the FAIL condition at `:419`, replace the `code` tests with `SITES_FAILED -gt 0`.
4. Install line (`:423-424`): keep the fields in order, add `cache=` after `home=` (both from the main site's row) and, on networks only, `sites=PASSED/TOTAL` before the result:
   `name<TAB>old -> new<TAB>status=S<TAB>home=CODE<TAB>cache=C<TAB>new_log_lines=N[<TAB>sites=P/T]<TAB>ok|FAIL`
   Then print `SITE_LINES` (networks), then the existing log text and restore lines.
5. Docs: the header comments (`scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh:9-13`, `scripts/deploy-sites.sh:27-34`, and the `usage()` range at `scripts/deploy-sites.sh:77` if needed), `RELEASING.md:22` and `RELEASING.md:134-137`. Each must say that on a network every site that is not archived, deleted or spam is loaded and fetched, with one line per site; that fetches use a unique query string; that `cache=` lists the response's cache headers; and that `WARN cached` means a cache answered anyway (one set to ignore query strings), so PHP did not run for that fetch. Add one `Developers:` entry at the top of `README.md` → `### Unreleased` and `changelog.txt` → `= Unreleased =`, ending "Plugins made from the starter get it with scripts/sync-core.sh."

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Each per-site load runs under its own `active_guard`, as the main-site load does now. The guard snapshots the stored activation list of every blog, and the network list, before the load and requires them unchanged afterwards (`RELEASING.md:24-37`). A concurrent change is reported and never overwritten, and a network is never restored automatically (`scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh:118-121`, `:166-171`). Fetches only read.
- **Migration/rollback:** The script migrates no data. Loading every site runs each site's settings upgrade during the deploy instead of on that site's next request; the plugin's upgrade code is the same either way. Restoring the plugin folder (the restore line is unchanged) does not undo settings on any site, which is already true for the main site today.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** The remote part always comes from the same checkout as `deploy-sites.sh` (`scripts/deploy-sites.sh:208`). Library users (`DEPLOY_LIBRARY_ONLY=1`) need `active_guard`, `wp_checked`, `wp_bare`, `log_files` and `install_name` to keep their arguments and behaviour; the new helpers only add. The install line keeps its fields in order. Per-site lines use the 4-space indent of the existing log and restore lines. The `list` (dry-run) output does not change.
- **Idempotency/retry:** Running `--apply` again with the same tag reinstalls and checks again. Each fetch's query string is unique (run stamp, process ID and a counter), so no fetch can be answered from a cache entry that an earlier fetch filled. Settings upgrades run once per version.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** When a site's load or status read fails, or its home page answers 5xx or not at all, the remaining sites of that install are still checked. The install then prints FAIL and its restore command, and the host run moves on to the next install, as now. A kind or site list that cannot be read fails the install with the restore line.
- **Run time:** Each site adds six WP-CLI runs (five for the guarded load, one for the status) and one fetch of up to 30 s. On the host where this was seen, the deploy did 16 installs in about 2 minutes and home pages answered in under 9 s, so a 12-site network adds about one to two minutes. There is no cap.

### Complexity Impact

- **Target function:** `apply_one` in `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`
- **Current line count:** 72 lines (361-432); the threshold is 100
- **Estimated growth:** about +45 lines if the pass is written inline
- **Projected post-change:** about 117 lines inline, which is over the threshold
- **Action required:** Extract the helpers first: `site_urls()` (~15 lines), `home_check()` (~20) and `check_sites()` (~40). `apply_one()` then stays under about 80 lines.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash -n scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh && bash -n scripts/deploy-sites.sh
scripts/lint.sh shell
DEPLOY_LIBRARY_ONLY=1 bash -c '. scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh && declare -F active_guard wp_checked wp_bare site_urls home_check check_sites >/dev/null'
scripts/deploy-sites.sh --help
```

Runtime check. It is ad hoc, on disposable Docker sites only, and adds no test files (the same kind of check PR #476 ran):

1. `scripts/test-site.sh up --multisite` creates a disposable subdirectory network with sites `/` and `/two/`, with the plugin network-active. Its first line names it: `Starting a disposable WordPress ... (NAME)...`. The Docker network is `NAME`, the files volume `NAME-wp` and the web container `NAME-web` (`scripts/lib/docker-wordpress.sh:62-70`). `scripts/test-site.sh url` gives `http://127.0.0.1:PORT`.
2. A container cannot reach `127.0.0.1:PORT`, so point the network at the web container's name, the reverse of `scripts/test-site.sh:196-197`: `scripts/test-site.sh wp search-replace '127.0.0.1:PORT' 'NAME-web' --all-tables`, then `scripts/test-site.sh wp config set DOMAIN_CURRENT_SITE 'NAME-web'`. The brief author has not run this step. If it does not work, find another way to give the container a reachable URL; do not add flags or environment variables to the scripts for testing.
3. `scripts/build-release.sh --out <tmp> --quiet` prints the zips' paths. Use `<slug>-X.Y.Z.zip`, take its SHA-256 with `shasum -a 256`, and use its X.Y.Z as VERSION. The CLI image runs as uid 33, so make `<tmp>` and the zip world-readable, as `scripts/test-site.sh:170-171` does for its zips.
4. Run the remote part the way `apply()` runs it on a server: `docker run --rm --network NAME --user 33:33 -v NAME-wp:/var/www/html -v <tmp>:/deploy:ro -v "$PWD/scripts/lib:/remote:ro" -e DEPLOY_WEB_ERROR_LOG=wp-content/debug.log wordpress:cli-php8.3 bash /remote/deploy-remote.sh apply <slug> /var/www/html VERSION /deploy/<zip> <sha> /tmp/backups`. Expect `zip SHA-256 on the host: ok`, the install line with `sites=2/2` and `ok`, two `site` lines, and exit status 0.
5. Make site two fail. Write `wp-content/mu-plugins/deploy-check.php` into the site (for example on stdin to `docker exec -i -u www-data NAME-web sh -c 'mkdir -p wp-content/mu-plugins && cat >wp-content/mu-plugins/deploy-check.php'`, as `scripts/lib/docker-wordpress.sh:19` writes `.htaccess`) with `<?php if ( 2 === get_current_blog_id() && ! defined( 'WP_CLI' ) ) { throw new RuntimeException( 'deploy check' ); }`, and rerun step 4. Expect site two `home=500 ... FAIL`, the install line FAIL with its restore line, and exit status 1. Repeat without `&& ! defined( 'WP_CLI' )`: expect site two's guarded load to fail. Remove the file.
6. Run `scripts/test-site.sh down`, then `scripts/test-site.sh up` (single site), then steps 2-4 (the `search-replace` alone is enough for step 2). Expect one install line, no `site` lines and `cache=none`. Then `scripts/test-site.sh down`.

- **Surface mapping:** `bash -n` and `scripts/lint.sh shell` cover every changed shell file. The `DEPLOY_LIBRARY_ONLY` line covers the library-compatibility hazard and the new helpers. `--help` covers the edited usage header. Steps 4-5 cover the per-site loads under `active_guard`, the network site lines, the FAIL policy, the restore line and the exit status. Step 6 covers the single-site regression.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required. The change is one script library plus its docs; no shared config, root tooling or release infrastructure changes.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused functional verification passes: `scripts/lint.sh shell` and runtime steps 1-5
- [ ] WIP commit created before broad gates: `wip: per-site deploy checks`
- [ ] Evidence-triggered broad verification then run: not required, for the reason given above

### Safety-Stop Recovery

- **Original objective:** The deploy checks every site of each multisite network, and every home fetch bypasses page caches.
- **Preserved user directions:** No host names, site names, server folders or private repository names in this public repository, its commits, PRs or comments.
- **Trigger and evidence:** Not triggered.
- **Completed and verified:** Nothing yet.
- **Remaining acceptance criteria:** All of them.
- **Unsafe route not to repeat:** Never run `--apply`, or the remote part, against a real host or site to verify this change.
- **Next safe route:** If Docker is unavailable or keeps timing out, finish the static checks, mark the runtime check `UNVERIFIED` in the PR, and keep the PR open for a runner with Docker. Unchecked work never counts as complete.
- **Resume condition:** A runner with a working Docker.
- **Owner and status:** The worker. Not triggered.

### Scope Boundaries

Initial implementation map. Directly necessary adjacent integration follows `reference/worker-discipline.md` "Integration scope recovery": document and verify the minimal corrected scope before editing. Explicit exclusions and hard boundaries remain binding and require a separate authorized brief-owner decision.

**Hard boundaries:**

- Verify only on disposable Docker sites, never on a real host or site.
- This repository is public, so add no host names, site names, server folders or private repository names (AGENTS.md → What belongs here).
- Do not add page-cache purging; that is #515.
- Do not change how `active_guard()` checks or restores activation lists.
- Do not commit a new test harness, and add no test-only flags or environment variables.

**AI brief owner:** The maintainer's interactive aidevops session that filed this issue, and otherwise Pulse terminal-blocker recovery.

**Recovery:** Preserve the current PR and use the structured runtime request and Pulse intake in `reference/worker-discipline.md` when local recovery is unsafe.

### Files Scope

- `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`
- `scripts/deploy-sites.sh`
- `RELEASING.md`
- `README.md`
- `changelog.txt`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On a disposable two-site network, `deploy-remote.sh apply` prints the install line with `sites=2/2` and `ok`, then one indented `site` line per site with status, home code and cache headers.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: manual
    prompt: "Runtime step 4 output is recorded in the PR: one install line with sites=2/2 and ok, and two site lines."
  ```

- [ ] A fatal error on the second site only, on its front end or in its WP-CLI load, fails that install: the site line and the install line say FAIL, the restore line is printed and the exit status is 1, while the main site's line passes.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: manual
    prompt: "Runtime step 5 output (both variants) is recorded in the PR."
  ```

- [ ] Every home fetch uses a query string unique to the fetch, and the output shows the final response's cache headers, or `none`. A cache `hit` is reported as `WARN cached` and does not fail.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "deploy-check="
    path: "scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh"
  ```

- [ ] Network sites that are archived, deleted or spam are neither loaded nor fetched.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "spam=0"
    path: "scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh"
  ```

- [ ] Regression: a single-site install still prints one line, with the same fields in the same order plus `cache=`. A 4xx is still reported only. The dry-run (`list`) output is unchanged. Sourcing the file with `DEPLOY_LIBRARY_ONLY=1` still runs nothing and still defines `active_guard`, `wp_checked` and `wp_bare`.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "DEPLOY_LIBRARY_ONLY=1 bash -c '. scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh && declare -F active_guard wp_checked wp_bare >/dev/null'"
  ```

- [ ] No host name, site name, server folder or private repository name is added to the repository or the PR.

    method: manual
    prompt: "Review the diff and PR body for private names or paths."
  ```

- [ ] Changed-file lint is clean: `scripts/lint.sh shell`.

    run: "scripts/lint.sh shell"
  ```

## Context & Decisions

- The per-site work goes in the remote part, which runs on the host. `deploy-sites.sh` only downloads, verifies, copies and runs it.
- Each site gets its own `active_guard` rather than one guard around all sites. That keeps the failing site exact, at a cost of five WP-CLI runs per site, which is accepted.
- A unique query string observes past the cache without changing it. Purging changes what visitors get, needs commands for each cache plugin, and is #515's job.
- Networks get per-site lines while single sites keep one line, so the common case prints no more than before.
- Archived, deleted and spam sites are skipped because they do not serve their home pages by design.
- The main site comes first, from `option get home` as today, so the install line keeps describing the main site.

title: Core CSS: documented public classes for plugins, a nav helper, and a Core class names check that warns only on internal classes and restyling
body:
## What

Give the core stylesheets a documented list of public classes: the classes a plugin made from the starter may use. Make the release preflight's **Core class names** check read that list, and add a nav helper so plugin screens stop copying core markup.

## Why

In a plugin made from the starter (SEO Pro Stats 1.17.1), `scripts/preflight-release.sh` reports about 197 **Core class names** warnings. They fall into three groups. Only the third is a real risk:

1. **Settings tabs following the settings screen's look.** For example, `{css}-card`, `{css}-cards`, `{css}-section`, `{css}-badge`, `{css}-field` and `{css}-setting` in a feature's settings tab. These should look like the core screen. Only `{css}-panel-note` and `{css}-panel-note--warning` are allowed today (#503).
2. **The colour-mode switch.** Theme CSS keyed on `.{css}-dark`, the class the starter's colour-mode controls set (#456). Plugins are meant to hook into it.
3. **The plugin's own components restyling core classes.** For example, a React app that defines its own `.{css}-badge` or `.{css}-card` rules, which a starter sync can silently change.

The docs also contradict each other:
- The `render_header()` docblock in `admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php` tells a plugin's own screens to use `<div class="wrap {css}-wrap">`, `<div class="{css}-main">` and `<nav class="{css}-nav">` / `{css}-nav__tab`.
- `STANDARDS.md` (the rule that plugin-own code must not reuse `{css}-wrap`, `-header`, `-nav`, `-subnav`, `-main`) forbids those same classes, and preflight warns when they're used.

So a plugin that follows the documented page shell is warned for doing so.

The hint is also unhelpful: every warning suggests `.{css}-<screen>-nav`, whatever the class is.

The aim is to treat the core CSS like a library with a public API. Plugins use public classes freely, never restyle them, and give their own components their own names.

## How

1. **Define the public list in one place the check can read.** Either a new core file (for example `scripts/core-public-classes.txt`) or marker comments in the core stylesheets (for example `/* public */` before a rule block). Keep #503's two classes. Add, after checking each one in `admin/css/wpstarter-admin.css`, `wpstarter-header.css` and `wpstarter-theme.css`:
   - Page shell: `{css}-wrap`, `{css}-main`, `{css}-nav`, `{css}-nav__tab`, and any `__group` / `__end` parts the nav uses.
   - Settings components: `{css}-card`, `{css}-cards`, `{css}-section`, `{css}-badge` and its modifiers, `{css}-field`, `{css}-setting`.
   - Colour mode: `{css}-dark`.

   Leave anything you're unsure about internal, and say so in the PR.
2. **Update `check_core_class_names()` in `scripts/preflight-release.sh`.**
   - Read the list instead of the hard-coded `feature_api_classes` array.
   - In PHP, JS and TS markup, warn only for classes not on the list.
   - In plugin CSS, still warn when a selector *defines* rules for any core class, public or not. Restyling a public class is the conflict. A selector that only uses `.{css}-dark` as an ancestor is allowed.
   - Make the hint name the class, for example "use a plugin-own name such as `.{css}-<screen>-badge`".
3. **Add a nav helper.** Add one to `WPStarter_Admin_Page` (`admin/includes/class-admin-page.php`) or `WPStarter_Admin_Manager`. It takes the sections and the shown one, and prints the `{css}-nav` markup with `is-active` and `aria-current`. Then plugin screens don't copy it. Update the `render_header()` docblock to point to it.
4. **Docs.**
   - In `STYLING.md`, add a "Classes a plugin may use" section that lists the public classes. Say that a plugin's own components use their own sub-prefix (`{css}-<screen>-*` or `{css}-app-*`), and never restyle a public class.
   - Rewrite the matching rule in `STANDARDS.md` to agree, so the two docs no longer contradict each other.
   - State that changing or removing a public class is a changelog item that plugins must act on.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `scripts/preflight-release.sh`
- EDIT: `STYLING.md`
- EDIT: `STANDARDS.md`
- EDIT: `admin/includes/class-admin-page.php` and/or `admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php`
- NEW (if this route is chosen): `scripts/core-public-classes.txt`, listed in `scripts/core-files.txt`
- EDIT: changelog entry, following the starter's existing release notes

## Reference pattern

#503 (the `panel-note` allowlist) and #487 (the original check). Keep their tests and behaviour for internal classes.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` passes.
- In the starter, `scripts/preflight-release.sh` has no Core class names warnings.
- In a plugin made from the starter, after syncing core:
  - markup using `{css}-card`, `{css}-badge`, `{css}-nav` or `{css}-panel-note` doesn't warn;
  - a plugin stylesheet that defines `.{css}-badge { … }` still warns, with a hint that names the class;
  - `.{css}-dark .{css}-app-card { … }` doesn't warn.
- A plugin screen built with the new nav helper looks the same as the settings screen's tabs (before/after screenshot in the PR).

## Follow-up

Plugin-side renames happen in each plugin after this ships. SEO Pro Stats has its own issue.

title: Core class names: public .wps-code and .wps-main--wide, and no warnings from comments or the dark palette
body:
## What

Release preflight's Core class names check (#524) warns on 12 lines in SEO Pro Stack (wpallstars/seoprostack#873). Some of the warnings come from gaps in the starter: a core class plugins are meant to use is not on the public list, a page-shell change has no public modifier, and the checker reads selectors inside multi-line comments. Fix those here, then sync to the plugins.

## Findings

1. `.{css}-code` (`admin/css/wpstarter-admin.css:234`, dark rule in `wpstarter-theme.css:193`) is a styled `<pre>` block for feature output, such as server rules to copy. No core code uses it, and it is not in `scripts/core-public-classes.txt`, so every plugin that prints it gets "reuses internal core class". It should be public.
2. A tab that needs the whole width of the screen, such as a grid of plugin cards, has no public way to drop `.{css}-main`'s `max-width: 1200px` (`admin/css/wpstarter-header.css:323`). Plugins restyle `.{css}-main.{css}-tab-<slug>`, which the check flags (correctly).
3. Multi-line comments: `check_core_class_names()` in `scripts/preflight-release.sh` strips `/* … */` only within one line. A comment line such as ` * Math's own selectors behind html.{css}-dark, so it wins.` is read as a selector list, and `.{css}-dark` is reported as restyled.
4. `html.{css}-dark { … }` on its own, setting a plugin's dark palette (custom properties, `color-scheme`, the page background) on screens the core theme does not style, is reported as restyling `.{css}-dark`. STYLING.md says to use the class only as an ancestor, but the palette has to go on `<html>`, as core's own `wpstarter-theme.css:11` does.

## How

- `scripts/core-public-classes.txt`: add `wps-code` (with a comment: feature output, a code block to copy) and `wps-main--wide`.
- `admin/css/wpstarter-header.css`: add `.wps-main--wide { max-width: none; }` after `.wps-main`.
- `admin/includes/class-admin-page.php` `panel()`: add an optional `$wide` argument that adds `wps-main--wide`. `admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php`: pass `!empty($tabs[$slug]['wide'])`, and document the optional `wide` tab key in the `wpstarter_admin_tabs` docblock and in `get_tabs()`'s `@return` shape. Own screens print `<div class="wps-main wps-main--wide">`.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh` `check_core_class_names()`: for CSS files, read each file at the release ref once, blank out comments but keep line breaks, and check the uncommented line. Do not report a rule whose subject is `.{css}-dark` alone when its declarations are only custom properties, `color-scheme`, `background` or `background-color`.
- `STYLING.md` → Classes a plugin may use: add `{css}-main--wide` to the page shell (tab key `'wide' => true`), `{css}-code` (feature output), and the palette rule for `html.{css}-dark`. `README.md` (tab keys, if listed) and changelogs as usual.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` passes.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline --no-docker` in the starter: no new warnings.
- In wpallstars/seoprostack, after `scripts/sync-core.sh --from <starter checkout>`, its preflight has no Core class names warnings once its own changes from #873 are in.
- A tab with `'wide' => true` gets `wps-main wps-main--wide`; other tabs' markup is unchanged.

### Files Scope

- `scripts/core-public-classes.txt`
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh`
- `admin/css/wpstarter-header.css`
- `admin/includes/class-admin-page.php`
- `admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php`
- `STYLING.md`
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`

title: fix(deploy): LiteSpeed Cache purge reported as failed after updates (5 s loopback timeout)
body:
## What

`scripts/deploy-sites.sh --apply` reports `WARN purge failed` on sites where LiteSpeed Cache's page cache purge did run.

LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.2's `wp litespeed-purge all|blog <id>` queues the purge, then delivers it with a request to the site's `admin-ajax.php` (`Core::kick_purge_queue()`, `wp_safe_remote_get()` with WordPress's 5 second timeout) and exits 1 with "Could not notify the web server to purge." when that request fails. Right after a plugin update the site's first PHP requests recompile the updated code, and on the owner's Hostinger host `admin-ajax.php` then took 4.6–7 s (measured with curl from the host during the SEO Pro Stack 1.3.76 rollout), so 6 of 17 installs and 7 network sites reported a failed purge. The queue stays in the database and the next request delivers it, so pages were purged late rather than not at all, but the rollout cannot tell.

## Fix

In `load_code()` of `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`, give requests to `admin-ajax.php` a 30 second timeout (`http_request_args`) before running the purge command; `WP_CLI::runcommand()` with `launch => false` runs in the same process, so the filter applies to LiteSpeed Cache's delivery request.

## Verification

- `bash -n scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`, `scripts/lint.sh`.
- Next rollout: `purged=yes` on the installs that reported `WARN purge failed`.

title: Settings: ordered multi fields that people drag into order
body:
## What

A `multi` setting always stores its values in the options' order (`sanitize_multi()` in `includes/class-{prefix}-settings.php`), so a feature cannot keep a list whose order matters, such as share buttons, where the plugin it replaces lets people drag them into order. Case: SEO Pro Stack's Social sharing imports Kadence Simple Share's networks, and the owner's sites use five different orders, all lost on import (wpallstars/seoprostack#923).

## How

- `includes/class-{prefix}-settings.php`: a schema key `ordered` (multi only): `sanitize_multi()` keeps the chosen values in the order given.
- `admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php` `render_multi()`: an ordered field lists the chosen choices first, in their saved order (so the checked boxes, top to bottom, are that order), each with a drag handle button beside its label, and a line of help.
- `admin/js/{prefix}-admin.js`: jQuery UI Sortable on `[data-{css}-ordered]` rows by the handle; the up and down arrow keys on a focused handle move a row; either saves the field as a change does.
- `admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php`: `jquery-ui-sortable` as a dependency of the admin script; `admin/css/{prefix}-admin.css`: the handle and rows.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`.
- A test site with an `ordered` multi field: drag a row and reload (order kept); arrow keys on a handle (order kept, focus stays on the handle); a non-ordered multi field still stores in the options' order.

title: Settings: same() compares ordered multi fields in order
body:
## What

`WPStarter_Settings::same()` (`includes/class-wpstarter-settings.php`) compares lists in any order: it sorts both before comparing. For a multi setting marked `ordered` (added in #538, PR #539), the order is the value, so a change that only reorders it counts as no change:

- `replace_site_values()` (Make every site the same, multisite) skips copying a network value that differs from a site's only in order.
- `WPStarter_Network_Differences::card_differs()` does not list the site as different.
- `WPStarter_Network_Sites::seed()` and `run_saving_work()` miss order-only changes.

Found by CodeRabbit on wpallstars/seoprostack#924, where SEO Pro Stack's Social sharing networks are the first ordered field.

## How

- `same($a, $b, $key = '')`: when `$key` names an `ordered` field in the schema, compare the lists in order (still as strings, scalars only); otherwise keep sorting.
- Pass the setting key from the callers: `replace_site_values()`, `WPStarter_Network_Sites::seed()` and `run_saving_work()`, `WPStarter_Network_Differences::card_differs()`.
- Changelog Unreleased line; plugins get it with `scripts/sync-core.sh`.

## Verify

- `scripts/lint.sh` passes.
- On a test site (through SEO Pro Stack after sync): `same(['x','facebook'], ['facebook','x'], 'social_sharing_networks')` is false; without the key, or for a non-ordered multi key, it is true.

## What

An ordered multi field (`ordered => true`) with more than 12 choices gets both `is-long` and `data-wps-ordered`. `.wps-checkboxes.is-long` sets `display: block` and `columns: 16em auto`; the ordered rule only sets `flex-direction`, `align-items` and `gap`, which have no effect on a block box. title: deploy-sites.sh: single-site FAIL lines omit the reason
body:
## What

`scripts/deploy-sites.sh --apply` shows only a bare `FAIL` on a single-site install line when that site's load, status read or home check fails. The reason is kept for network `site` lines, which single sites never print, so the operator gets a restore command and nothing to act on. SEO Pro Stack hit this in its 1.3.86 rollout (a transient guarded-load failure) and fixed it in its copy of the core file (wpallstars/seoprostack#964).

## How

Take the fix into the starter's `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh` (a core file), unchanged:

- `wp_checked` and `active_guard` keep WP-CLI's exit code instead of returning 1.
- `check_sites` captures the guarded load's stderr, keeps the full text on stderr, and records a short printable reason (exit code and the last three lines, at most 300 characters) as `MAIN_REASON` for the first site.
- `apply_one` prints `FAIL: <reason>` on single-site install lines; the restore command still prints for any `FAIL*` result.

Docs: `RELEASING.md` step 5, changelog Unreleased in `README.md` and `changelog.txt`.

## Verification

- `shellcheck scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`, `bash -n`.
- SEO Pro Stack's PR tested the same code against controlled WP-CLI responses (Bash 5.3 and 3.2).
- After merge, `scripts/sync-core.sh --check` in SEO Pro Stack no longer reports the file as changed here.

title: sync-core.sh: support add-on plugins without an admin screen
body:
## What

`scripts/sync-core.sh` (and the weekly `.github/workflows/starter-sync.yml` that runs `--check`) cannot serve an **add-on plugin**: a plugin made from the starter, or from a plugin made from it, that runs only beside its parent plugin, has no admin screen of its own and deliberately drops the starter's admin and settings files.

Observed in one such add-on (private, so not named here):

1. **Identity fails.** `plugin_identity` (`scripts/lib/plugin.sh:99-103`) reads the CSS prefix only from the `wrap <css>-wrap` class in `admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php`. The add-on has no such file, so every script that calls `plugin_identity` stops: `plugin: no "wrap <css>-wrap" class in admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php at HEAD` / `sync-core: cannot tell which plugin this is`. Its weekly Starter sync run has failed on this since its admin screen was removed, so it no longer opens the sync issue, and starter fixes (deploy, preflight, RELEASING.md) silently stopped reaching it until they were copied by hand.
2. **Dropped files would come back.** The list of core files comes from the starter at REF (`sync-core.sh:120`), so even with identity fixed, a sync would class every dropped admin/settings file as `missing` and add it back.
3. **Parent names.** The add-on's shared files (scripts, docs) carry its parent plugin's names, not its own, because they were copied from the parent, and its `scripts/core-files.txt` still lists the parent's files. A sync with the add-on's own names would rename them.

## How (proposed; pick the smallest that covers all three)

- `scripts/lib/plugin.sh`: when the admin manager is absent, fall back to another source for `PLUGIN_CSS`, such as the prefix of the classes in the plugin's own `scripts/core-public-classes.txt` (`<css>-wrap` is its first page-shell class), or an explicit plugin-own setting. Keep the error when neither exists.
- `scripts/sync-core.sh`: let a plugin list core files or folders it deliberately does not carry (for example a plugin-own `scripts/core-files-skip.txt`, or `# skip` lines in an own block of `scripts/core-files.txt`); skipped paths are neither `missing` nor added, and `--check` lists them once as skipped.
- Optionally, a way to take names from a parent plugin (for example `--names-from DIR`, or a plugin-own setting naming the parent's main file), for add-ons whose shared files use the parent's names.
- Document it in `DEVELOPMENT.md` → Starter sync and `STANDARDS.md` → Structure (add-ons), and keep `scripts/rename-plugin.sh` working on a fresh copy (`AGENTS.md` → What belongs here).

## Verification

- In the starter: `scripts/sync-core.sh --check` in a throwaway clone with `admin/` removed and the new skip list/fallback in place reports the skipped files and no `missing` for them; without the skip list, behaviour is unchanged.
- In the starter itself and an ordinary plugin: `scripts/sync-core.sh --check` output is unchanged.
- In the add-on (maintainer, after merge): `scripts/sync-core.sh --check` runs, and the weekly Starter sync passes or opens its issue instead of failing.
- `shellcheck` on changed scripts; CI passes.

title: preflight-release.sh: Core files note says to pass --from, which preflight rejects
body:
## What

`scripts/preflight-release.sh` → `check_core_files()` runs `scripts/sync-core.sh --check` and, when no starter checkout is found, prints sync-core's message as a note:

```
Core files

```

But preflight has no `--from` option: `scripts/preflight-release.sh --from DIR` stops with `preflight: unknown argument: --from`. The hint is right for `sync-core.sh`, not for preflight. In a linked worktree (a plugin checked out under a worktrees folder) the default path is next to the worktree, so this note shows on every run there.

`sync-core.sh` already takes the checkout from `STARTER_DIR` (`plugin_env STARTER_DIR …`, `scripts/sync-core.sh` around line 262), so preflight works with `STARTER_DIR=DIR scripts/preflight-release.sh`; nothing says so.

## How

In `scripts/preflight-release.sh`:

1. Either accept `--from DIR` and pass it to `sync-core.sh --check --from DIR` in `check_core_files()` (add it to the header comment that `usage()` prints, lines 2 to 18), or
2. keep the options as they are and make the note preflight's own: "not compared: no starter checkout at …; clone it there, or set STARTER_DIR=DIR".

Option 1 matches sync-core and is the smaller surprise. Mention it in `DEVELOPMENT.md` where preflight is described, and in `changelog.txt` and `README.md` under Unreleased.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `scripts/preflight-release.sh`
- EDIT: `DEVELOPMENT.md`
- EDIT: `changelog.txt`
- EDIT: `README.md`

title: test-site.sh: label sites for aidevops teardown and add prune for orphaned sites
body:
## What

Make `scripts/test-site.sh` sites clean themselves up when the worktree that made them is removed, and add a `prune` command for state folders whose site is gone.

## Why

Observed on 2026-10-29 on the maintainer's Mac: 16 orphaned test sites (32 containers, 16 networks, 32 volumes, some 13 days old) from seoprostack, seoprodirectory, seoprocookieconsent and seoproanalytics, plus 96 state folders under `~/.local/state/wpallstars-test-sites/`, 80 of them for sites already gone. They were removed by hand.

Cause:

- `up` keeps a site until someone runs `down`. Sessions and workers that end, stop early or hand off skip `down`.
- The site name and label digest come from `slug:branch:checkout path`, so once the worktree is removed nobody can run `down` for that site.
- aidevops already removes Docker resources when a worktree is removed (`worktree-helper.sh remove`/`clean`, post-merge cleanup), and the pulse reaps by TTL. It only touches resources carrying its six `sh.aidevops.*` owner labels. `test-site.sh` adds only `wpallstars.test-site=<digest>`, so `docker-resource-helper.sh report` counted **0 labelled** of 57 containers.
- `down` removes only `site`, `credentials` and the zip, so it leaves the folder and its `zips/` directory behind.

`plugin-check.sh` and `update-test.sh` remove their own sites on exit and don't pile up, but should get the same labels so a crashed run is still cleaned up.

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `scripts/lib/docker-wordpress.sh`: replace the single optional `DOCKER_LABEL` with a label array (for example `DOCKER_LABELS=()`) used by `docker_prepare_core`, `docker_start_site` and every `docker run`/`network create`/`volume create` there.
- EDIT: `scripts/test-site.sh`: build the label array, add `prune`, make `down` remove the empty folder, record ownership in state.
- EDIT: `scripts/plugin-check.sh`, `scripts/update-test.sh`: use the same label array (check how each sets `DOCKER_LABEL` today with `rg -n DOCKER_LABEL scripts`).
- EDIT: `DEVELOPMENT.md` (test-site section around lines 49-84): document `prune` and the automatic cleanup.

All four scripts are core files (`scripts/core-files.txt`), so change them here and sync to plugins with `scripts/sync-core.sh`.

### Implementation steps

1. **Owner labels.** Keep `wpallstars.test-site=<digest>` (it is what `down` lists by). When `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/docker-resource-helper.sh` is executable, also add its labels, read line by line into the array as `tools/containers/disposable-resources.md` → "Starting a labelled stack" shows:
   `docker-resource-helper.sh labels --worktree "$root" --ttl-hours 168`
   A long TTL suits `up` sites, which are meant to live across sessions; `plugin-check.sh`/`update-test.sh` can use the default. Without aidevops the script must behave exactly as now (the starter is public; do not require aidevops). The six labels are `sh.aidevops.owner=1`, `repo`, `ref`, `worktree`, `created`, `ttl-hours`.
2. **Ownership in state.** Add the checkout root and branch as extra lines in `$TMP_DIR/site` (read as data, as `load_site` does now; keep accepting the old three-line files).
3. **`down`.** After removing the known files, `rmdir "$TMP_DIR/zips"` and remove the folder itself only when it is then empty (no `rm -rf` of a computed path; `finish` removes `lock`, so do the final `rmdir "$TMP_DIR"` there after `down`).
4. **`prune`** (new command, does not need to run inside the site's checkout): for each folder in the state home, skip it if it has `lock/`; remove its labelled Docker resources and the folder when its recorded checkout path no longer exists, or when the folder has no Docker resources with its `wpallstars.test-site` digest. Delete only by exact label listing, as `down` does. Print what it removed; `--dry-run` lists only. Folders from before step 2 have no recorded path: treat them as orphaned only when no resource carries their digest (the digest is the folder name's suffix only in part, so compute it the same way or store it).
5. **Notice.** At the end of `up`, print how many other test sites are running (count distinct `wpallstars.test-site` label values) and suggest `prune` when there are more than, say, 5.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `scripts/test-site.sh`
- EDIT: `scripts/lib/docker-wordpress.sh`
- EDIT: `scripts/plugin-check.sh`
- EDIT: `scripts/update-test.sh`
- EDIT: `DEVELOPMENT.md`

### Hazards

- Never prune a site another session is using: honour `lock/`, and never remove a site whose checkout still exists and has running containers.
- Keep Bash 3.2 compatible (macOS); arrays with `${arr[@]+"${arr[@]}"}` as the file already does under `set -u`.
- Paths with spaces in worktree roots must survive the label array.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docker inspect` of a new `up` site's containers, network and volumes shows the six `sh.aidevops.*` labels when aidevops is installed, and only `wpallstars.test-site` when the helper is absent (test with `PATH`/`HOME` pointing away, or a flag the script honours).
- `docker-resource-helper.sh teardown --worktree <removed worktree> --dry-run` lists that site's resources after the worktree is removed.
- `test-site.sh down` leaves no folder behind for that site.
- `test-site.sh prune --dry-run` lists orphaned folders and resources; `prune` removes them, skips locked folders and keeps live sites.
- `scripts/plugin-check.sh` and `scripts/update-test.sh` still pass and leave nothing behind.
- ShellCheck clean; `DEVELOPMENT.md` documents `prune`.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck scripts/test-site.sh scripts/lib/docker-wordpress.sh scripts/plugin-check.sh scripts/update-test.sh
scripts/test-site.sh up && docker ps --filter label=sh.aidevops.owner=1 --format '{{.Names}}'
scripts/test-site.sh down && ls "${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/wpallstars-test-sites"
scripts/test-site.sh prune --dry-run
```

## Relevant files

- `scripts/test-site.sh:58-99` (`resources`, `down`, `finish`), `:156-175` (name, label, state folder)
- `scripts/lib/docker-wordpress.sh:23-70`
- aidevops label contract: `~/.aidevops/agents/tools/containers/disposable-resources.md`; teardown on worktree removal: `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/worktree-helper-integration.sh` (`docker_resource_auto_teardown`)

title: fix: deploy-sites.sh --apply takes a per-plugin lock on the host, so overlapping rollouts cannot overwrite each other
body:
## What

`scripts/deploy-sites.sh --apply` has no lock on the SSH host. Two runs for the same plugin can install into the same plugin folders at the same time. On 2026-10-29 a run deploying v1.3.100 to every install on one host overlapped with a second session's per-install v1.3.99 runs (`--parent <one folder>`, started 36 s later):

- 13 single sites passed as `1.3.98 -> 1.3.100 ... ok` in the first run, then the second run reinstalled 1.3.99 over them. The first run's report no longer matched the sites.
- On one network, the 1.3.99 install landed between the first run's install and its version check, so it printed `1.3.98 -> 1.3.99 ... FAIL` plus a restore command. Running that command would have put the network back on 1.3.98 while the other run was still active.

## How

- EDIT `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`: in `main()`, before any install in `apply` mode, take a per-plugin lock on the host, for example `mkdir "$HOME/.{slug}-deploy/.lock"` with a file inside holding the PID, tag, start time and parent pattern. Remove it on exit with a `trap`. If the lock exists and its PID is still running, stop before installing and print who holds it (tag, start time, parent). If that PID is no longer running, take the lock over with a warning. Use `mkdir`, not `flock`, so it works on shared hosts without util-linux. The `list` (dry run) mode takes no lock and prints a line when a run is active.
- EDIT `scripts/deploy-sites.sh`: report the lock message and exit non-zero. Document it in the script's header comment.
- EDIT `RELEASING.md` (shared file), under Scripts → `deploy-sites.sh`: one sentence on the lock and on what to do when a run is active.
- Core files: change these in the starter first, then sync to plugins (`STANDARDS.md` → Agent docs).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`
- EDIT: `scripts/deploy-sites.sh`
- EDIT: `RELEASING.md`

## Verification

- `shellcheck scripts/deploy-sites.sh scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh` reports nothing.
- On a test host or Docker: start `--apply` with `--parent` set to one folder. While it runs, start a second `--apply`. The second stops before installing and names the first run's tag. A dry run (no `--apply`) prints that a run is active and still lists the installs.
- Kill the first run with `kill -9`, then run again: it warns about the stale lock and goes ahead.

title: Report a problem: let site AI assistants draft reports that administrators send to the product's maintainers
body:
## What

Every plugin made from the starter, and every theme made from the child theme
starter, gets one shared way for a site's AI assistant to report a problem or
an improvement in that product, approved by a site administrator before it
leaves the site.

Today an AI looking at an installed plugin finds nothing telling it where to
report: the release zip leaves out `AGENTS.md` and `docs/`, and the header's
**Support** link points at GitHub issues, which a private repository's users
cannot open.

## How

- New shared component `includes/wpallstars-reports/` (`load.php` and
  `class-wpallstars-reports.php`), on the shared GitHub updater's pattern: each
  copy registers its version, and on `after_setup_theme` (so themes' copies
  count too) only the newest copy loads, once, for every product on the site.
- Products register through the `wpallstars_report_products` filter. The
  starter's bootstrap (`includes/class-wpstarter.php`) adds the plugin from
  `WPStarter_Setup::header_links()['support']`: a GitHub issues address sends
  reports to GitHub; `mailto:address` sends them by email to that address.
- AI agents draft only:
  - ability `wpallstars/report-problem` (WordPress 6.9+, `manage_options`), and
    `wpallstars/reports` to read drafts and what happened to them;
  - `wp wpallstars report create|list|show|delete|products`.
- Administrators review, edit and send in **Tools → Report a problem**:
  - email: sent with the site's own mailer (`wp_mail()`), with the site's
    address, versions and the sender as Reply-To;
  - GitHub: a prefilled new-issue link, opened with the administrator's own
    account, with the site's address, email addresses, IP addresses, paths and
    anything that looks like a key taken out first.
- The header's **Support** button opens that screen for the plugin.
- `README.md` → a short **Report a problem** section, which ships and shows in
  the Read Me tab, so assistants reading the installed plugin find it.

### Files Scope

- includes/wpallstars-reports/load.php
- includes/wpallstars-reports/class-wpallstars-reports.php
- includes/class-wpstarter.php
- admin/includes/class-admin-page.php
- scripts/core-files.txt
- uninstall.php
- STANDARDS.md
- README.md
- readme.txt
- changelog.txt

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`, `scripts/smoke-test.sh`.
- On a test site: create a draft with `wp wpallstars report create`, see it in
  Tools → Report a problem, send it (email channel) and check the mail log; for
  the GitHub channel, check the link's body has no site address.
- WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4: the abilities are skipped, the rest works.

title: deploy-sites.sh: refuse to install a release older than the installed version unless --allow-downgrade
body:
## What

`scripts/deploy-sites.sh --apply` (remote half: `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`, `apply_one()`) installs the requested tag even when an install already has a **newer** version, and reports it as `ok`. Make it refuse a downgrade per install unless the operator passes a new `--allow-downgrade` flag.

## Why

Observed on 30 October 2026 with SEO Pro Stack, whose copy of these core files is synced from this repository (`scripts/core-files.txt`, `scripts/sync-core.sh`). Two sessions were rolling out releases to the same host. One checked an install at 1.3.105 and, about two minutes later, ran `deploy-sites.sh --tag v1.3.106 --apply` for it. Meanwhile the other session had installed 1.3.107. The output line was:

```
<install>	1.3.107 -> 1.3.106	status=active-network	purged=1/2	home=200	...	ok
```

The install ran the older release until it was noticed and 1.3.107 was installed again about a minute later. A downgrade can also reverse a settings upgrade the newer version has already run. Nothing in the tool warned. The version check before the run was stale by the time it applied, so the guard has to sit in `apply_one()` at install time, not in a dry run.

## How

1. `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`, `apply_one()` (around line 536, after `before="$(plugin_version "$main")"` and before the backup): if `before` is non-empty and is newer than `want`, compared with `sort -V` (`printf '%s\n%s\n' "$want" "$before" | sort -V | tail -n 1`; no `version_compare`, since the host runs bash and coreutils only), print `"%s\tFAIL: has %s, newer than %s; not installed (--allow-downgrade to install anyway)\n"`, set `FAILED=1` and `return 0`. If `before` equals `want`, keep the current behaviour: a reinstall is allowed.
2. Pass the flag through: `scripts/deploy-sites.sh` parses `--allow-downgrade` (document it in the usage header next to `--apply`, lines 5–21) and hands it to the remote `main()` as one more positional word, after the existing ones (see how `want` is passed at `main()` around line 626). The remote side defaults to refusing.
3. In `--dry-run`, mark each install whose version is newer than the tag (for example `newer than tag; --apply will refuse`), so the plan shows it.
4. Bump the starter's version and changelog in the usual way. Downstream plugins pick it up with `scripts/sync-core.sh`.

## Files

- `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`: `apply_one()`, `main()`, and the dry-run listing (`list_one()`, around line 365).
- `scripts/deploy-sites.sh`: option parsing and usage header.

## Verification

- `shellcheck scripts/deploy-sites.sh scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`: zero findings.
- Bash 3.2 syntax check: `bash -n` on both.
- Run the remote half against a temporary folder that has a fake `wp-content/plugins/<slug>/<slug>.php` with `Version: 9.9.9`, a stub `wp` on `PATH`, and an older `want`: it prints the FAIL line, exits 1, and never calls `wp plugin install`. With `--allow-downgrade` it goes ahead. With an equal or older installed version, behaviour is unchanged. No new test harness needed; a throwaway shell run is enough.
- Then sync into wpallstars/seoprostack and wpallstars/seoprodirectory with `scripts/sync-core.sh` (separate PRs in those repos).

### Files Scope

- `scripts/deploy-sites.sh`
- `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`
- `wp-plugin-starter-template.php`
- `README.md`
- `readme.txt`
- `changelog.txt`

title: Shared problem reports: echo escaped values from their own variables (Codacy echoed-request false positives)
body:
## What

Codacy (Opengrep rule `php.lang.security.injection.echoed-request`) reports
two "Echoing user input" findings in `includes/wpallstars-reports/class-wpallstars-reports.php`
on every plugin that syncs the shared problem reports and runs Codacy
(seen on wpallstars/seoprostack#1054 and wpallstars/seoprocookieconsent#106):

- line 771: the **New report** link, `esc_url(self::url('new', $product ? … : …))`,
  where `$product` comes from `$_GET['product']` through `sanitize_key()`;
- line 941: the details textarea, `esc_textarea($report ? $report['details'] : '')`,
  where `$report` comes from the `report` query argument through `self::get()`.

Both are already escaped (false positives: the rule only knows PHP's own
`htmlspecialchars()`/`htmlentities()`, not WordPress's escaping), but each
copy fails Codacy's PR gate once.

## How

- Compute the escaped value into its own variable before the `echo`
  (`$new_url = self::url('new', …);` then `echo … esc_url($new_url) …`;
  `$details = $report ? (string) $report['details'] : '';` then
  `echo esc_textarea($details);`), so the echoed expression no longer
  contains the request-derived variable. Output must stay identical.
- Raise the component version in `includes/wpallstars-reports/load.php` to
  `1.0.3`. Do not add suppressions or Codacy configuration.

### Files Scope

- includes/wpallstars-reports/class-wpallstars-reports.php
- includes/wpallstars-reports/load.php

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`.
- Test site: Tools → Report a problem, **New report** link with and without
  `&product=`; open a saved draft and check the details textarea shows its
  text (with `<`, `&` and quotes escaped).
- Copies: carry to the child theme starter and the plugins with
  `scripts/sync-core.sh` in their next sync.

title: deploy-sites.sh: refuse a --web-error-log in a missing folder; report a missing log file
body:
## What

`scripts/deploy-sites.sh --apply` must refuse a `--web-error-log` path whose folder does not exist on the host, and must say clearly when the log file itself does not exist yet. Today both cases pass silently, and the install line reports `new_log_lines=0` even though no web log was read.

## Why

Observed on 30 October 2026 in a plugin made from this starter (SEO Pro Directory 0.4.83 rollout). The operator typed the web log's absolute path with a wrong home folder. `deploy-sites.sh` accepted it and installed on five installs. Each line showed `new_log_lines=0`, but none of them read a web log. A manual check afterwards found no new lines, but the run's own evidence was empty.

In `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`, `log_files()` rejects a path that exists but is not a readable regular file. It accepts a path that does not exist, because a log file created during the install should still be counted. That rule is right for the file, but a missing **folder** cannot be a real log destination: PHP cannot create a log file in a folder that does not exist.

## How

1. EDIT `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`, `log_files()` (the `WEB_ERROR_LOG` branch, around the "not a readable regular file" check):

title: CI: a draft-time run cancels the ready-for-review run, so required checks stay skipped
body:
## What happened

On wpallstars/seoprostack#1089 a commit was pushed and the pull request was marked ready for review (`gh pr ready`) within the same second. Two CI runs started together on the same head:

- `pull_request` / `synchronize`: its payload still had `draft: true`, so `release` and `smoke` were **skipped** (`if: ... || !github.event.pull_request.draft`).
- `pull_request` / `ready_for_review`: payload `draft: false`, but it was **cancelled** by `concurrency: { group: ci-<PR number>, cancel-in-progress: true }`, because the other run joined the same group.

Result: the required checks "Release build, preflight and Plugin Check" and both "Smoke test" jobs showed as skipped, and the merge stayed `BLOCKED`. Re-running a run does not help: a re-run reuses its original event payload, so the draft-time run skips again. A fresh run (a new head commit, or closing and reopening the PR) was the only way through.

## Fix

Give draft and ready runs separate concurrency groups, so a ready run is never cancelled by a draft-time run of the same PR. In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.draft && 'draft' || 'ready' }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

Pushes to `main` and `workflow_dispatch` have no pull request, so they keep one `ready` group per ref. Consecutive pushes to a ready PR still cancel each other.

## Files

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (concurrency block, lines 25–27): a core file (`scripts/core-files.txt` lists `.github/`), so change it here in the starter first.
- Then sync it to each plugin made from the starter (seoprostack first) with the Starter sync in `DEVELOPMENT.md`.
- Optional: one line in the comment at the top of `ci.yml` (lines 5–6) noting that draft and ready runs are in separate groups.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` (actionlint covers the workflow).
- On a test PR: open it as a draft, then push a commit and run `gh pr ready` together. The `ready_for_review` run must complete with `release` and `smoke` run (not skipped, not cancelled), and the PR's merge state must not be `BLOCKED` by required checks.

title: CI: time limit on the draft-state request
body:
## What

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` → lint job → `Draft state` step (GH#592): the `curl` that reads the pull request's live draft flag has `--retry 2` but no time limit. A stalled GitHub response holds the lint job until its 15-minute `timeout-minutes`, and the fallback to the event's draft flag only runs when `curl` fails, so it never covers a stall. Found by CodeRabbit on a plugin's starter-sync PR (wpallstars/seoprocookieconsent#112).

## How

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: add `--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 20` to that `curl`, so with its two retries the step gives up within about a minute and uses the event's flag with the existing warning.
- `changelog.txt`: a Developers entry under Unreleased.

## Verify

- `scripts/lint.sh` (workflows: actionlint) passes.
- The PR's CI: the lint job logs `Draft: false.` and the release and smoke jobs run.

title: deploy-remote.sh: lock and downgrade-guard review findings
body:
## What

CodeRabbit reviewed `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh` (the 1.0.47 deploy lock and downgrade guard, GH#573 and GH#576) on two plugins' starter-sync PRs, wpallstars/seoprocookieconsent#112 and wpallstars/seoproanalytics#44. A maintainer read the code at starter `main` and sorted the findings below. Fix them here in the starter. Plugins get the fixes with `scripts/sync-core.sh`, which refuses plugin-only edits to core files.

### Confirmed, quick fixes

1. **`lock_live()` (around line 719): a `ps` failure counts as stale.** `args="$(ps -p "$pid" -o args= 2>/dev/null)" || return 1` treats any `ps -p` failure as "not live", for example BusyBox `ps` without `-p` or no readable process table. A second `--apply` then takes over a running deploy's lock with only a warning. Fall through to `kill -0 "$pid"` when `ps` fails. Keep the `*deploy-remote*` args check when `ps` works, since it rules out reused PIDs.
2. **`newer_than()` (around line 383): a prerelease of the target counts as newer.** `sort -V` sorts `2.0.0-rc1` after `2.0.0`, so an installed prerelease blocks the stable install unless `--allow-downgrade` is given. Return 1 (not newer) when `installed` is `"$want"-*`, before the `sort -V` comparison.
3. **`lock_take()` (around line 761): an owner-write failure looks like a lost lock.** When writing `owner` fails after `mkdir` succeeds, the run says it lost the lock and returns 3, and the ownerless directory stays. For two minutes, `lock_live()` then reports "another deploy is running" to every later run. Split the two cases. On a write failure, `rmdir "$dir"` (it removes only an empty directory), report that the lock could not be written, and return 2. On a PID mismatch, keep the directory and return 3, as now.

### Judgement calls (decide in the PR; no change is acceptable with a reason)

4. **`newer_than()`: an empty installed version is "not newer".** An unreadable `Version:` header lets `--apply` install with `--force` and no downgrade check. Option: return 2 (comparison failure, refused unless `--allow-downgrade`). Consider an unreadable header on a broken install, which a deploy should be able to repair.
5. **`lock_path()` (around line 683): the lock lives under `$HOME`.** SSH accounts with different home folders that reach the same WordPress folder take different locks. This is a documented design limit (`DEVELOPMENT.md`, `RELEASING.md`: `~/.{slug}-deploy/.lock`). A shared location needs a path every account can write to. Document the limit, or lock per installation root.
6. **`lock_break()` (around line 731): the takeover is not exclusive.** Moving the lock aside and then reading its PID leaves a window in which three concurrent runs can end with two installing at once. Fixes are a second takeover lock, or `flock` where the host has it. Weigh the cost against how likely three overlapping `--apply` runs of one plugin on one host are.

### Docs, confirmed (from wpallstars/seoprostack#1111)

7. **`RELEASING.md` (line 22, the `scripts/deploy-sites.sh` row): `--allow-downgrade` is missing.** `scripts/deploy-sites.sh` accepts it (its usage comment, line 22), but the synopsis leaves it out, and the description doesn't say that `--apply` refuses a release older than the installed version unless it is given. Add both, wording them to match items 2 and 4 as fixed.

## How

- `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`: items 1 to 3, plus items 4 to 6 as decided.
- `RELEASING.md`: item 7.
- `DEVELOPMENT.md` / `RELEASING.md` (deploy lock text): update if behaviour or a documented limit changes.
- `changelog.txt`: a Developers entry under Unreleased.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`
- EDIT: `DEVELOPMENT.md`
- EDIT: `RELEASING.md`
- EDIT: `changelog.txt`

## Verify

- `scripts/lint.sh` (ShellCheck) passes.
- Items 1 to 3 with a scratch copy of the functions in bash: `ps` replaced by a function that fails while the PID is alive keeps the lock live; `newer_than 2.0.0-rc1 2.0.0` returns 1; an unwritable `owner` file leaves no lock directory and returns 2.
- `scripts/deploy-sites.sh` dry run against a test site still lists sites and takes no lock.

title: CI: Docker Hub 429s still fail Plugin Check and smoke tests after the mirror (GH#501)
body:
## What

CI still fails on Docker Hub 429 (Too Many Requests) after GH#501 / #508. Make the image pulls in Plugin Check and the smoke tests survive a rate-limited runner, without needing a secret.

## Why (observed)

On 31 Oct 2026, starter-sync PRs in two plugins made from this starter failed Plugin Check and two of the four smoke tests. The code had no PHP changes, and the same sync passed in four other plugins.

- 21:23 UTC: `mariadb:10.6` and `wordpress:cli-php8.3` failed all three attempts in `pull_image` with `failed to resolve reference "docker.io/library/mariadb:10.6": unexpected status from HEAD request to https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/library/mariadb/manifests/10.6: 429 Too Many Requests`. One job got `You have reached your unauthenticated pull rate limit`.
- 21:56 UTC: re-running the failed jobs gave the same 429 on `mariadb:10.6` in one plugin.
- A second re-run passed. Each failure cost about 15 minutes of re-runs and waiting.

GH#501 added `scripts/ci-docker-mirror.sh`, which puts `https://mirror.gcr.io` in `registry-mirrors` on GitHub-hosted runners, and 3 pulls 20 s apart in `pull_image`. `DEVELOPMENT.md` already notes that a cache miss still falls back to Docker Hub. The errors name `registry-1.docker.io`, so either the mirror was not used or the mirror request failed or missed, and dockerd then reports the Docker Hub error. `mariadb:10.6` and `wordpress:cli-php8.3` are common official images, so a cache miss is unlikely. The 60-second retry window is also short next to a rate limit that lasts hours on a shared runner IP.

## How

These are core files (`scripts/core-files.txt`): change them here, and starter syncs carry the change to each plugin.

1. **Find the cause first.** In a failed job's log, check the **Docker Hub mirror** step (`scripts/ci-docker-mirror.sh`): did it run (`runner.environment == 'github-hosted'`), and does its `docker info` list `Registry Mirrors: https://mirror.gcr.io/`? Re-create a 429 if you can, for example with dockerd debug logging on a hosted runner, to see whether dockerd tried the mirror before Docker Hub. Record the finding in the PR.
2. **Pull official images from the mirror by name** when on CI. In `pull_image` (`scripts/smoke-test.sh:135` and `scripts/plugin-check.sh:89`, the same function in both), pull `library/` images as `mirror.gcr.io/library/<name>:<tag>` and `docker tag` them to the plain name. When that fails, use the existing plain `docker pull` with its retries. Turn this on only in CI (for example when `GITHUB_ACTIONS` is `true`, or with a new `*_IMAGE_MIRROR` setting that CI sets), so local runs are unchanged. Move the shared `pull_image` into `scripts/lib/docker-wordpress.sh`, which both scripts already source, rather than changing two copies.
3. **Optional Docker Hub login** in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, before the Plugin Check and smoke steps: log in only when repository secrets for it exist (for example `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` and `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN`), and skip it otherwise so forks still run. A logged-in pull has a much higher limit. Use the pinned `docker/login-action`, or `docker login --password-stdin`.
4. Update the CI section of `DEVELOPMENT.md` (lines 196-210): the explicit mirror pull, the fallback, the optional secrets, and that the mirror is for CI only.

Do not lengthen the retry wait to fix this: a runner IP's rate limit outlasts any sensible wait.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `scripts/lib/docker-wordpress.sh` (shared `pull_image`)
- EDIT: `scripts/smoke-test.sh`, `scripts/plugin-check.sh` (use the shared function)
- EDIT: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (optional login; mirror setting if used)
- EDIT: `scripts/ci-docker-mirror.sh` (only if step 1 shows it does not take effect)
- EDIT: `DEVELOPMENT.md`

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh shell` and `scripts/lint.sh workflows` pass.
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh`, `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4`, `scripts/smoke-test.sh --multisite` and `scripts/plugin-check.sh` work locally as before, with no mirror pull outside CI.
- The PR's CI log shows `mariadb:10.6` and the `wordpress:` images coming from `mirror.gcr.io`, and Plugin Check and all three smoke tests pass.
- `scripts/rename-plugin.sh` on a throwaway clone still lints, because core file names change (AGENTS.md → What belongs here).
